President Donald Trump boasted Sunday about winning another club championship trophy at his golf club in New Jersey, asserting that he won because he has “talent” that his competitors don’t possess.

On Truth Social, the president posted a video of his “winning shot” at Trump National Golf Course in Bedminster that landed him the club championship trophy in the Super Senior and Senior categories.

“I won with a score of 70, and am so honored in that, unlike the rest of the field, I’m given very little time to practice, because I’m focused on many other things. It’s called TALENT, and I have it, and they don’t!” Trump wrote.

While the president is an avid golfer and often gloats about his skills on the course, some have accused him of cheating, which Trump denies.

According to a video posted online, Trump won the Super Senior Men’s Club Championship, which is generally the category for men 65 years and older, as well as the Senior Men’s Club Championship, which is typically for men 50 years and older.

open image in gallery A screenshot from President Donald Trump's latest Truth Social post shows his 'winning shot' at his golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey ( realDonaldTrump / Truth Social )

Last year, the president won the same Senior Men’s Club Championship tournament, which the White House later posted about.

Trump also won both Senior and Super Senior championships in 2023 and announced it in a similar Truth Social post: “For some reason, I am just a good golfer/athlete - I have won many Club Championships, and it is always a great honor!”

But years of cheating allegations, dating back to before Trump’s first term, have haunted the president’s golf game.

In 2016, actor Samuel L. Jackson accused the president of cheating at golf. In 2018, LPGA player Suzann Pettersen was reported as saying the president “cheats like hell,” though Pettersen later denied making the comments.

Sports writer Rick Reilly even wrote a book on Trump’s alleged cheating in 2019, titled “Commander in Cheat.”

“At Winged Foot, where Trump is a member, the caddies got so used to seeing him kick his ball back onto the fairway they came up with a nickname for him: Pele,” Reilly wrote, referring to the Brazilian soccer star.

open image in gallery An online tracker of Trump’s golf outings estimated the president has spent 124 of his 559 days in office golfing ( Getty )

Last year, the cheating allegations were reignited after a video of Trump playing golf in Scotland went viral, appearing to show Trump’s caddy walking ahead of the president and dropping his ball closer to the fairway.

Earlier this year, the New York Times reported that the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a close ally of Trump, had insinuated Trump cheats at golf during a 2022 grand jury testimony.

“Some people say you may outdrive him, but you’re not going to outdrive his caddy. It is what it is.” Graham said when asked whether the president cheats at golf.

Ariana Grande will soon take a break from public life amid the ongoing discourse surrounding her health and body, her representative said Sunday.

Grande will be “taking a step back from visibility” following the completion of her Eternal Sunshine tour in London on September 1, the representative announced.

“She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” they told People magazine.

“This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.”

Grande will also no longer appear in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park with George, People has confirmed.

open image in gallery Ariana Grande has faced intense scrutiny about her health and body in recent years ( Getty )

open image in gallery The news of her withdrawal from public life comes just days after the release of her eighth studio album, petal ( AP )

The production was set to open at London's Barbican Centre next summer, with Grande due to star opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey.

A source close to Grande told People that she “cannot wait to support the brilliant team bringing this project to life.”

The news of Grande’s break from the public eye comes days after the release of her eighth studio album, Petal, which reignited the discourse surrounding her body and health.

British model, author and body positivity activist Charlotte Howard was among those to speak out following the release of Grande’s music video for “Petal” (the single of the same name from the new album) on July 31.

“I think it’s vital we discuss imagery/videos/content like these and the damage they can - and will - have on women and girls. WHAT YOU SEE HERE IS NOT NORMAL,” wrote Howard alongside stills from the music video.

“Over the past few weeks, as images of Ariana’s concert get plastered around online, I obviously see comments from worried fans, but I also see other people convincing others that she looks ‘healthy’, or that she has simply ‘lost puppy fat’. Some even make jokes about it.

“What I see is someone in desperate need of hospitalisation and care, and while I know it’s often impossible to help someone at this stage of anorexia, there HAS to be an immediate intervention.

“... I think it is absolutely appalling, from both a moral and capitalistic standpoint, to have released these videos and an album when this person needs psychiatric help and hospitalisation. The teams involved should be absolutely ashamed. ... I truly, truly hope she gets the help that she so desperately needs.”

Late last year, during the Wicked: For Good press tour, Grande issued a “loving reminder” to her fans and others to think before they speak.

On her Instagram Story, she reshared her 2024 interview with French internet personality Sally Poumbga, in which she was asked about beauty standards.

“I’ve been a specimen in a petri-dish since I was 17, so I’ve heard it all,” Grande said. “I’ve heard ‘what’s wrong’ with me, and then you fix it, and then it’s wrong for different reasons.

“I think in today’s society there’s a comfortability that we shouldn’t have, at all, commenting on others’ looks, appearance… what they think is going on ‘behind the scenes’ or health or how they present themselves,” she explained. “I think it’s dangerous, for both parties involved.”

For anyone struggling with the issues raised in this article, eating disorder charity Beat’s helpline is available 365 days a year on 0808 801 0677. NCFED offers information, resources and counselling for those suffering from eating disorders, as well as their support networks. Visit eating-disorders.org.uk or call 0845 838 2040

News.content:
Officials give update on In-N-Out shooting in Idaho

At least three people were killed and seven others were injured in a shooting at an In-N-Out in Idaho, officials confirmed as they released the name of the gunman — who they say died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The suspected gunman was identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, who died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound near the fast food chain in Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people located roughly 130 miles southeast of Boise, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks confirmed Sunday.

Those injured include two patients who were treated and released from the hospital and three who remain hospitalized in stable condition and two who are in critical condition. Authorities said they would not be releasing the identities of the deceased on Sunday.

However, police said they are “confident” that Williams acted alone.

One of the people killed was an associate at In-N-Out, the chain’s president, Lynsi Snyder, confirmed earlier Sunday.

Authorities also confirmed during Sunday’s press conference that an off-duty state trooper and citizen actively engaged the suspect by returning gunfire toward him.

The FBI has established a tip line for the public to submit photos and videos related to the shooting.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Bruno Guimaraes twist, Man Utd done deal, Vinicius Jr to Arsenal
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes appears to be closing in on a move to Arsenal from Newcastle United

All the latest transfer news with Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool among the Premier League teams looking to strengthen this summer

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Sunday, August 2.

The summer transfer window is full flow with several Premier League clubs beginning to ramp up their business. Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea have made a busy start to the window, while Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United loook set to follow suit.

Mikel Arteta's side look poised to make blockbuster moves for Vinicius Junior and Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners have reportedly set a day aside for a medical for the Magpies' captain, with reports claiming a bid in excess of £75m has been agreed.

It's been another summer of upheaval at Newcastle United with Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon leaving St. James' Park, with Eddie Howe also leaving the club last week. Lewis Hall and Joelinton are also being linked with moves away from the club, in what would be a huge blow for incoming head coach Matthias Jaissle.

Elsewhere, Liverpool are being linked with a big money move Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The French champions may ease their stance, however, with the signing Maghnes Akliouche and a move for Ajax winger Mika Godts.

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Arsenal handed Bruno Guimaraes boost as Newcastle change their transfer stance
Sports.content:
Arsenal handed Bruno Guimaraes boost as Newcastle change their transfer stance

Newcastle United have been insistent that their captain Bruno Guimaraes is not for sale, but a transfer to Arsenal appears to be in the works and the Magpies are looking for a replacement

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is heading to the exit at Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

Newcastle United have reportedly identified a potential replacement for Bruno Guimaraes as their captain edges closer to joining Arsenal.

‌



The Magpies are undergoing a summer of upheaval, with Guimaraes likely to follow Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali out the door after Eddie Howe left his position as manager. Having sold Gordon and Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively, Newcastle had been insistent that Guimaraes was not for sale at any price.

‌



But interest from Premier League champions Arsenal has not gone away and the Brazil international now looks set to make the move to London. The Times have reported that Guimaraes could undergo a medical on Monday with a deal worth £80million edging closer.

‌



Guimaraes sent an emotional farewell message to Howe and is keen to join Mikel Arteta's side. It seems that Newcastle have now been forced to face reality, with the team scouring the market for a potential replacement in midfield.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Every Premier League summer transfer as Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool splash the cash READ MORE :

Corriere dello Sport report that they are ready to challenge Leeds for Inter Milan star Petar Sucic and are prepared to offer between €35m and €40m (£30m and £34m) for his services. The Croatia international has emerged as a key player for Inter and the Italian giants don't want to lose him.

‌



The 22-year-old made 50 appearances for Inter in all competitions last season, contributing four goals and four assists. The Serie A champions value the midfielder at around €45m (£38.4m) and could play Newcastle and Leeds off against each other to drive up the price.

Newcastle have plenty of experience of missing out on transfer targets in recent windows so know how costly they can be. This summer Johan Manzambi went to Aston Villa and Victor Munoz to Liverpool, while last summer Hugo Ekitike and Benjamin Sesko were the most notable misses.

View 2 Images Petar Sucic played for Croatia at the World Cup (Image: Steve Russell/Toronto Star via Getty Images)

‌



Frustrations around losing key players and a lack of incoming transfers is understood to have been one of the reasons behind Howe's departure. Matthias Jaissle is poised to leave Al-Ahli replace Howe and will have a difficult job in rebuilding after the departures of key players.

Arsenal, meanwhile, want Guimaraes to increase their depth in central midfield alongside the likes of Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Martin Odegaard. The Gunners have agreed to sell Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m in preparation for Guimaraes' arrival.

A £34m deal to sign winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge to replace Leandro Trossard is the only major signing of the summer window for Arsenal. But they are chasing Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior as well as Guimaraes and manager Arteta has promised more to come.

‌



"We are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," Arteta said after their 4-1 pre-season friendly win over Girona. "We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it.

"The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Sports.content:
Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan

Liverpool's hopes of signing PSG star Bradley Barcola have been boosted after reports suggest the French club are closing in on Ajax forward Mika Godts as his potential replacement

View 2 Images Ajax have stepped up their efforts to sign a replacement for Bradley Barcola (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly stepping up their efforts to sign Ajax star Mika Godts, which could hand Liverpool a boost to their hopes of signing Bradley Barcola. The Reds have been heavily linked with signing the France international this summer as they look to strengthen their wide forward options before the transfer window closes.

‌



Barcola’s current deal with PSG is set to expire in the summer of 2028, and it has been widely reported that the 23-year-old does not want to put pen to paper on an extension at the Parc des Princes. There have even been suggestions that Barcola is open to the idea of a move to Anfield, which has given Liverpool encouragement that a deal could be completed.

‌



It has been reported previously that Liverpool are expected to hold talks with PSG over a deal to sign Barcola, with the winger apparently valued at around £140million. That said, separate reports have suggested that Liverpool are optimistic about negotiating a fee closer to £100million for the France international.

Godts predominantly operates on the left wing for Ajax, and should the deal go through, it would probably fuel additional suggestions that Barcola might be heading towards the exit. Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut

Alejandro Garnacho has completed a loan move from Chelsea to Aston Villa and the former Manchester United winger has appeared to take a dig at his former employers

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho left Chelsea for Aston Villa (Image: Chelsea Football Club, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Alejandro Garnacho has claimed he is enjoying football again in an apparent dig at former club Chelsea. The Argentinian made his Aston Villa debut against Indonesia All Stars as Unai Emery's side ran out 3-1 winners but the 22-year-old couldn't resist a swipe at the Blues.

‌



Garnacho joined the Europa League holders on a season-long loan with a conditional obligation to buy for £43million, should Villa opt to trigger it. It appears no love has been lost with his former employers after suggesting he had an unhappy time at Stamford Bridge.

‌



Xabi Alonso made the attacker surplus to requirements after being appointed as the permanent manager. Garnacho, who left Manchester United under a cloud last summer, has sparked another bitter dispute after departing a club.

‌



Taking to social media following their 3-1 victory over Indonesia All Stars, Garnacho said: "First start after three months.

Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend READ MORE :

"Happy to be enjoying football again. One percent every day. Thanks Indonesia."

The attacker's stint at Old Trafford concluded on a bitter note before his initial switch to Stamford Bridge failed to come off in January 2025. Garnacho lost favour under Ruben Amorim and was dropped from the squad for the victory over Manchester City, while his omission from the Europa League final starting XI prompted a post-match outburst.

‌



United will be monitoring developments closely as Garnacho prepares for his maiden season in the West Midlands. Michael Carrick's outfit would be entitled to 10 per cent of any future transfer fee for the 22-year-old and should the buyout clause be activated, Villa will be obliged to pay £43million for his signature.

.JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Garnacho endured a torrid debut season in the capital, during a chaotic period for the Londoners that saw a string of managerial changes. Enzo Maresca had been keen to bring the United winger to the club but departed in January after 18 months at the helm. Liam Rosenior was subsequently appointed as his replacement, yet his time in charge proved brief, with the axe falling after just 106 days

Alonso was confirmed as permanent boss this summer following Calum McFarlane's stint as caretaker. Yet in the Spaniard's very first move at Stamford Bridge, he showed the Argentine the door.

Emery now faces the task of reviving Garnacho's career after a bruising spell at both United and Chelsea. The Europa League-winning manager said: "We are delighted with Alejandro. He is so talented, young and he showed us his wish to help our project. We are really happy."

Sports.title: 10th-tier side release bizarre Jadon Sancho statement as Man Utd flop looks for new club
Sports.content:
10th-tier side release bizarre Jadon Sancho statement as Man Utd flop looks for new club

Jadon Sancho has been training by himself since being released by Manchester United at the end of June and his latest move has prompted a non-league side to release a statement

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho has been training at Flixton FC (Image: PA)

Non-league side Flixton have felt compelled to release a statement stating that Jadon Sancho is not in talks to sign for them after speculation on social media.

‌



Sancho is currently a free agent, having been released by Manchester United on July 1. The 26-year-old left the club alongside Casemiro and Tyrell Malacia and is yet to find a new team in the summer transfer window.

‌



His £73million transfer from Borussia Dortmund did not work out at Old Trafford, with just 12 goals coming in 83 appearances over the past five years. Sancho spent time on loan with Borussia Dortmund and Chelsea before playing last season with Aston Villa.

‌



With no club, Sancho has taken to training solo at Flixton FC in Greater Manchester. In a video for the 10th-tier club's social media channels he praised their facilities, leading to some tongue-in-cheek speculation that he could drop down to non-league.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“You’ve got a nice layout here," Sancho said. “It’s my first time around this area, and it's the first time I’ve seen a nice pitch [in this area] apart from United and City."

‌



The club, who have Rhodri Giggs - the brother of United legend Ryan as their assistant manager - have decided to clarify the situation. In a statement, Flixton owner Christopher Garcia said: "Over the past few days, we've seen a number of posts and comments circulating regarding Jadon Sancho's visit to Flixton FC.

"To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions. He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.

"We're proud that the quality of our pitch and facilities made Flixton a place where a player of his calibre felt comfortable training, and he is welcome to train at Flixton FC whenever he wishes.

‌



View 2 Images Jadon Sancho is looking for a new club (Image: PA)

"During his visit, Jadon was nothing but professional, humble, and generous with his time. After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

"Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of. He deserves respect for both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.

‌



"We thank Jadon for choosing Flixton FC as a place to train and wish him every success in the next stage of his career, which will undoubtedly be at a level far above where we currently compete. Our doors will always be open to him."

Sancho is yet to field much interest in his services, with Qatari side Al-Rayyan one of few to make an enquiry. The winger is said to be open to moving to the Middle East, where the Saudi Pro League is a possibility, or staying in Europe.

Sports.content:
Preston vs Barcelona friendly cancelled hours before kick-off for bizarre reason

Preston North End's pre-season friendly with Barcelona has been cancelled at the 11th hour, with the Championship side set to face the Spanish giants in a behind-closed-doors match at St. George's Park

View 2 Images Barcelona are in the United Kingdom for pre-season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Barcelona's pre-season friendly against Prest North End has been called off just one day before it was meant to take place. The La Liga giants were scheduled to face the Championship side in a behind-closed-doors friendly at St. George's Park.

‌



Hansi Flick's side are currently in the United Kingdom preparing for the new season, and played Birmingham City last week, losing the match on penalties. The hope of being able to get another intense runout in for Karim Adeyemi and co, while much of the squad is yet to return from their break following the World Cup, failed to come to fruition, however.

‌



Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Preston were unwilling to risk more senior stars for the match and instead proposed a game with their under-21 squad, being unable to fill the places for a full senior squad. The suggestion was declined by Barca, who have decided to hold a normal training session in its place.

‌



Preston take on Huddersfield Town in the League Cup in the coming days and were not willing to risk further injuries as a result. Barcelona will soon return to Spain, earlier than planned, to continue their preparations.

They will take on British opposition, with two further pre-season matches lined up against Udinese and Nottingham Forest next weekend. Flick's side will travel to Italy to play in the three-team tournament, with three 45-minute matches taking place at the Bluenergy Stadium in Udine.

Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is set to leave Old Trafford this summer, with the Turkey international expected to join La Liga side Celta Vigo on a loan deal

View 2 Images Michael Carrick faces a busy summer as Manchester United manager (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Altay Bayindir is getting closer to completing a move away from Manchester United this summer. La Liga club Celta Vigo are set to sign the Turkey international.

‌



United signed Bayindir from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, but the shot-stopper has made just 17 appearances during his three years at Old Trafford. Bayindir joined United to serve as the understudy to Andre Onana, which was the case for his first two years at the club.

‌



That changed last summer when Senne Lammens signed for the Red Devils and went on to become the club’s new No.1 goalkeeper. Bayindir's prospects at United have been shrouded in doubt for quite some time, particularly following the club's decision to bring in Karl Darlow on a free transfer earlier this summer.

‌



Man Utd star claims club can win Premier League after mood change under Michael Carrick READ MORE :

It has now been reported by Metropolitano that Celta Vigo are on the brink of signing Bayindir on a loan basis from United, with the deal said to be almost entirely wrapped up in quick fashion. The same report suggests that the La Liga club are hopeful of formally announcing the agreement to sign Bayindir next week, with the goalkeeper anticipated to join his new squad at a training camp in Italy.

A separate report from Spanish publication AS claims that the 28-year-old is expected to undergo a medical to complete his move to Celta Vigo on either Sunday or Monday. Our sister title The Manchester Evening News reported on Saturday that Celta Vigo are leading the chase to secure Bayindir's signature, with the goalkeeper appearing increasingly likely to depart the club in the coming days.

Speaking after the win, Carrick told MUTV: “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

It remains unclear precisely when Bayindir's United departure could be announced, though all indications suggest the goalkeeper's stint at the club is drawing to a close, albeit via a loan arrangement.

Sports.title: 'Missed opportunity' for Hull and Woad for maiden major win
Sports.content:
Charley Hull and Lottie Woad will be left cursing a "missed opportunity" to claim a maiden major win at the AIG Women's Open, according to Dame Laura Davies.

Hull and Woad finished four strokes behind eventual champion Shiho Kuwaki (-5) in tied-sixth as both failed to mount a final-round charge on Sunday at Royal Lytham & St Annes.

Woad started the day at three under but fell away when posting her first over-par round of the week, while Hull couldn't build on a birdie start as two double-bogeys at three and seven sunk her challenge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes.

"They'll both see this as a missed opportunity because five under has won it," Sky Sports Golf's Davies, a four-time major winner, said of Hull and Woad.

"Charley played a little bit in and out, whereas Lottie was really solid, she just didn't hole enough putts."

Speaking to that point, Hull had 17 birdies over the week, trailing only world No 1 Nelly Korda's 19, who finished one stroke better in a tie for fourth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charley Hull's major hopes were derailed after a nightmare start to the final day of the AIG Women's Open.

But Hull also posted 12 bogeys, in addition to the two costly doubles in her final round which, if removed, would have also secured her a place in the play-off at five under.

"Charley made a few too many mistakes," Davies added. "And that's just the way she plays golf; she goes full out attack.

"She was pretty disciplined this week, but I think she'll think, 'I was only four back and I should have been in there right at the death.'"

'Major win will surely happen for Woad'

Woad posted a bogey-free 69 in her opening round, but struggled to make further inroads on the leaderboard with rounds of 71 and 70 to follow before fading on the final day.

Image: Lottie Woad posted a two-over 73 on Sunday to see her AIG Women's Open challenge fall away

There's plenty of positives for the 22-year-old, however, with a fifth top-10 finish for her fledgling career that sees her debut Solheim Cup appearance for Team Europe next month.

"Woad didn't roll in enough putts," Andrew Cotter said on commentary. "But she continues this remarkable run of three Women's Open Championships played and a third top-10.

"Again she shows her quality and a major will surely happen for her in the future - she's only 22 years old.

"It's another top-10 but just not quite there on this occasion."

What's next?

The Ladies European Tour stays in England for the PIF London Championship, beginning Thursday at the Centurion Club, while the LPGA Tour takes a week off before the Standard Portland Classic from August 13-16. Get Sky Sports or stream golf and more with no contract.

Sports.title: Blue Bolt confirms superiority over Precise at Deauville
Sports.content:
Blue Bolt continued her faultless campaign with victory in the Prix Rothschild at Deauville.

Runner-up to Fallen Angel in the Sun Chariot at Newmarket at the end of last season, Andrew Balding's filly has taken her game to another level this term with a comeback win in Listed company at Goodwood followed by big-race triumphs in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Falmouth at Newmarket.

The four-year-old was renewing rivalry with the July course runner-up, Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes heroine Precise, and at one stage it looked like the latter may take her revenge in the hands of Ryan Moore.

But Blue Bolt was doing her best work at the finish under Colin Keane and lunged late to claim a seventh win from 10 career starts, with Sir Mark Prescott's Coronation Stakes fourth Moon Target bettering that result with a fine effort to finish third.

Balding told Sky Sports Racing: "She's some filly, she really is - and Colin gave her a wonderful ride. It wasn't very comfortable watching it, I thought we were beat in the last furlong, but he's judged it to perfection.

"She's got great physical strength for a filly, that's her biggest quality, and she's got great desire as well. A big thank you to the team at home and Alfie Redman who rides her every day. She's not easy and likes to take control of things, but he's really mastered her this last six months and done a great job of it.

"She likes to get on with it, she's a powerful traveller and knows her strength, so it's about harnessing that in the right direction."

Blue Bolt now looks set to bid for further Group One success in Ireland, with her trainer adding: "The great thing about her is she's effective on any ground, which is a big help.

"We always felt the Matron Stakes at Leopardstown (September 12) was her race this year and we won't lose sight of that for anything prior to that."

Sports.title: Dunkley leads Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds as MI London remain winless
Sports.content:
Sophia Dunkley's 56 off 33 balls fired Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds in an impressive victory by five runs in The Hundred at Trent Bridge.

Opener Dunkley's imperious innings was aided by a useful contribution from her international team-mate Nat Sciver-Brunt (33 off 25) and a cameo from Bess Heath to leave the Rockets with a middling - but defendable - score of 139-7 after their 100 balls.

Australia star Ash Gardener (1-18) delivered for the home side, taking the early wicket of opener Bryony Smith (10 off 12) and limiting the top-order scoring of Jess Jonassen (19 off 18) and Phoebe Litchfield (24 off 22) to leave SunRisers Leeds well behind the required run-rate at 73-3 off 64 balls.

Image: Phoebe Litchfield managed 24 off 22 before being dismissed by Charley Phillips

Annabel Sutherland, though, reignited hope for the batting side with a brilliant 59no off 30 deliveries, but it was too little too late for the visitors as some tidy bowling by Kim Garth (0-26) at the death - despite a last-ball maximum by Sutherland - meant the Rockets held on and secured an important victory.

The win consolidates their strong position as they remain second in the table, while SunRisers Leeds, languishing in seventh, take another damaging blow to their Eliminator chances.

Manchester Super Giants leave MI London winless

Manchester Super Giants consolidated their third-place position in The Hundred with a six-wicket win over MI London.

MI London, still without a win and planted firmly at the foot of the table, lost the toss and were asked to bat, and it was imperative that they got off to a decent start in the absence of Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who has been ruled out the remainder of the tournament.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Blue Bolt and Precise clash again in Prix Rothschild
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Sunday with Flat action from Chester, Yarmouth and Deauville, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.40 Deauville - Star fillies Blue Bolt and Precise lock horns again

A red-hot renewal of this Group One Prix Rothschild at Deauville where Blue Bolt and Precise renew their rivalry.

Andrew Balding's Blue Bolt saw off Precise when landing a first Group One success in the Falmouth at Newmarket last month and bids to confirm that form under Colin Keane. A dominant winner on that occasion, the market believes she can follow up and land a four-timer.

Balding said: "She seems in good nick and if she repeats the performance from Newmarket she will take a lot of beating.

"She's been a star this year and the only factor is she has never travelled far from home to run before. But if she takes the travel in her stride then she should hold every chance of continuing her winning run."

Aidan O'Brien saddles Precise, herself a four-time Group One scorer, with Ryan Moore in the plate. An impressive winner of the Irish 1000 Guineas, she took the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot before failing to land a blow on Blue Bolt. Sent off the odds-on favourite that day, it will be fascinating to see if she can reverse the form.

O'Brien said: "She's in good form, she was stood in the gates a little bit long the last day and lost a couple of lengths and turned her head a little bit.

"Hopefully she won't do that the next day and give away those lengths. It's hard to do that at somewhere like Newmarket, especially at the July meeting where you are going straight down. We're happy with everything she's doing and looking forward to seeing her again, she's been a special filly for us so far."

Moon Target has two lengths to find on her fourth behind Precise at the Royal meeting, while Green Spirit might appreciate the drop back to a mile.

A deep contest has several with each-way claims including Karl Burke's 1,000 Guineas runner-up Evolutionist.

3.20 Chester - Unbeaten Lifeplan heads the field

Declan Carroll's Lifeplan faces eight rivals as he bids to remain unbeaten in a cracking edition of the Listed Queensferry Stakes at Chester.

Last year's Gimcrack champion has not been seen since landing that prestigious prize back in August and his connections are hoping he can make up for lost time. Stall nine will make life a bit trickier for jockey Zak Wheatley however.

Song Of The Clyde is a top performer on his day and showed all his ability when taking the Listed Carnarvon Stakes at Newbury. Below his best the last twice, he will not want conditions to be too quick.

Hugo Palmer fields Fitzella and Ardisia who are both closely matched on the pick of their runs, while Calico Blue steps up in class for Roger Varian.

12.56 Deauville - Woot Woot, Nicely and Queen Of The Day clash

A strong edition of the Sky Sports Racing Prix Six Perfections where a host of in-form two-year-old clash over seven furlongs.

Christopher Head has never hidden his admiration for Woot Woot and she justified that reputation when winning impressively at Saint-Cloud and she warrants respect on this grade.

Queen Of The Day defeated Woot Woot on debut before chasing home the exciting Avec Toi on her second start and she will find this an easier task.

British raider Nicely stepped forward from her debut to win comfortably at Hamilton and adds further intrigue to this splendid opener.

Best of the rest

1.32 Deauville - Group Three contest with Light Of Dawn representing Wathnan Racing and Karl Burke. Jorolina and Kosuma look useful.

3.05 Deauville - Group Three where Elle Eclipse and Lefteye feature. Evita has good form behind Diamond Necklace. William Buick rides Symbol Of Majesty.

10.09 Saratoga - Grade Two Glen Falls - rescheduled with Survie and Gezora fancied.

3.52 Chester - Power Fizz and Monarch's Gold involved alongside Roman Dragon.

3.08 Yarmouth - Valuable novice.

Sports.title: Staveley-led consortium agrees deal for minority stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
Vanessa Gold has confirmed she has agreed to sell her stake in the club to a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.

Gold, who succeeded her father David as joint-chair of the Hammers following his death in 2023, has a deal in place with a group headed by Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners for her family's 25.1 per cent holding.

However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Image: Former Newcastle co-owner Staveley's consortium is set to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the club

"Amanda Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, PCP Capital Partners along with Ashland Forest Capital Partners can confirm they have agreed the purchase of the Gold family's 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United," the Staveley-led consortium said in a statement.

"A legal binding agreement has been signed.

"This sale agreement, though, remains subject to a pre-emption process under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"No further comment will be made whilst the ongoing legal process takes its course."

Sky Sports News further understands Staveley, Ghodoussi and their consortium have brought together considerable funds.

Kretinsky voices displeasure at decision

In June, the club announced that co-owner Daniel Kretinsky was set to become West Ham United's largest shareholder after agreeing a deal to buy the Gold family's stake in the club.

The statement issued in June said they hoped to finalise the transaction within a couple of weeks, but that milestone has yet to be reached.

Kretinsky was due to increase his shareholding to 43 per cent, exceeding the current 38.8 per cent owned by David Sullivan, who has since released a statement in response to the latest development, expressing his disappointment over the Gold family's decision to sell their shares. It read:

"The agreement we had reached with the Gold family in June provided stability for the club at a crucial time.

"Today's [Saturday] announcement does the opposite.

"We will always act in the best interests of West Ham United and are reviewing all of our options, including exercising our pre-emption rights in full."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of West Ham's pre-season friendly against Stevenage

Gold said in a statement: "As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint-chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023.

"Whether as a youth-team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father's priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

"On June 12, Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

Image: The consortium is led by Staveley and her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, alongside PCP Capital Partners

"Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham.

"While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club's best interests, as my father did and would expect of me."

Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club's rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on August 16.

West Ham said in a statement: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from joint-chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation. Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

"The club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."

Warrington Wolves moved up to fourth in the Betfred Super League table after recovering from a lacklustre start to claim a comprehensive 48-18 win at Castleford Tigers .

Having lost four of their last six matches, including three in a row on the road, Warrington were made to pay for an error-strewn first 20 minutes as the Tigers went 16-6 ahead at the OneBore Stadium.

But Matty Ashton, Toby King and Toafofoa Sipley touched down to turn the tide and put Warrington 24-18 in front at half-time, and James Harrison and Leon Hayes extended the Wolves' lead after the break.

Ashton scored again, taking his tally to five tries in two matches against Castleford this year having bagged a hat-trick when Warrington claimed a 72-6 victory in March, before Ben Currie scored.

While Castleford were stuffed by rivals Wakefield last weekend, they claimed a shock win over Leeds in their last home match and Warrington head coach Sam Burgess had warned they would be no pushovers.

On this occasion, they could not find the defensive intent required to stop Warrington on their push for a spot at the top end of the top six.

They went 12 points ahead after Saints failed to deal with Hunter's lofted kick, Nikau Williams touching down and Bennison making it 28-16, but Robertson's brilliance allowed Tristan Sailor to feed Welsby to complete a length-of-the-field move which was converted by Hastings.

Sports.title: Pressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-election
Sports.content:
European countries are planning to increase the pressure on Gianni Infantino with a mass withdrawal of letters supporting his re-election as Fifa president.

Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup, which was largely scuppered when Uefa member associations threatened to boycott future Fifa competitions. The mood remains febrile and there is a widespread appetite around Europe to ensure that he is quickly removed from his post.

Now a groundswell of national governing bodies are discussing the formal withdrawal of their support for Infantino in a bid to hasten his resignation, with announcements likely in the coming days. Before last week’s crisis unfolded all of Uefa’s 55 members apart from Germany, Romania and Norway had written letters to endorse Infantino’s candidature next March, with a fourth term for the Swiss viewed as a fait accompli.

A simultaneous withdrawal has been mooted but there is also the possibility member associations could remove their backing one by one. Doing so would effectively amount to a vote of no confidence and increase the pressure on Infantino to resign. Fifa must be notified by any country wishing to recall their letter.

Discussions continue with countries in other confederations. Despite the failure of his Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, a number of countries in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) publicly backed Infantino over the weekend. Sources within European football have questioned whether those federations have been made fully aware of the level of ­dissent facing Infantino.

After the financial powerhouse of Qatar backed Infantino on Saturday, smaller Asian associations Sri Lanka and Kuwait offered their public ­support on Sunday. The AFC rarely votes en masse however, and it is possible that some associations unhappy with Infantino could rally to the European cause.

As the Guardian revealed in July, more than 200 of Fifa’s 211 members have provided letters of endorsement for Infantino. Fifa is understood to have applied heavy pressure upon those wavering even though his tenure did not appear endangered at the time. Many backed him despite privately offering misgivings about his presidency but, in Europe and beyond, patience has run out.

Efforts to identify a candidate to replace Infantino are being stepped up. Anyone put forward for the election would require significant levels of support outside Europe, particularly from the AFC and the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, Concacaf. Gathering quickly around a suitable contender could be key to persuading Infantino that his position is untenable.
