Infantino appears determined to stay on, and is believed to be ­lobbying individual member associations across the globe to ensure he retains their support. Both the ­Confederation of African Football and the South American confederation, Conmebol, are fully behind Infantino however, leaving Asia and North America as the crucial battlegrounds as Uefa members seek a new leadership at Fifa.

Sports.title: The five big beasts are gone: who will be the Premier League’s next alpha manager? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
This used to be a land of giants. This used to be a land where big men fought. This used to be a land where Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsène Wenger tussled, then José Mourinho joined the fray. This used to be a land where Jürgen Klopp made Pep Guardiola reconsider, and he changed his style and won anyway.

Not any more. Next season will be the first since the inaugural Premier League in 1992 not to feature any of the five big managerial beasts – not Ferguson, not Wenger, not Mourinho, not Klopp and not Guardiola.

What’s come over our great land? The Premier League is still our home, but where have all the heroes gone? Where’s the man who ruled by fury? Or the man who made virtues of broccoli and sobriety? Where’s the man who made the conference room the pitch? Where’s the gegenpressingmeister, or the cold philosopher of the positional game? Now they take a man who instigated some interesting pressing patterns and they call him a regular hero. Where are the men who are willing to play the game?

You don’t have to be a nostalgist in the vein of Bill Anderson to think that the Premier League looks a little diminished. Régis Le Bris took over at Sunderland two summers ago and already he is the fourth longest-serving manager currently at a Premier League club. While his quiet authority impressed last season, the understated Breton is no one’s idea of a main character. And it’ll take a while before the meeting of the two longest-servers, Mikel Arteta and Unai Emery, looks like a clash of the titans, even with the twist that Emery was Arteta’s predecessor at Arsenal.

Tottenham appointed Roberto De Zerbi in March and, the promoted sides excepted, he has already been a Premier League manager longer than 11 of his rivals. All long-running dramas go through this process. Major characters move on, new ones arise. At least they are easier to tell apart than in House of the Dragon: they don’t all have the same hair, and they are not all bafflingly interrelated. Still, it will take time for the new breed to become familiar. Quirks have to be learned, strengths and weaknesses understood.

View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi has the charisma of a leading figure. Photograph: Robbie Stephenson/PA

The result is that this season looks as hard to call as any in living memory. Perhaps the Premier League has entered its Arsenal era and Arteta will soon squat like a giant toad across English football. But retaining the league is difficult, particularly given the emotional outpouring that inevitably comes with ending a lengthy drought. Neither Declan Rice nor Bukayo Saka looked especially fresh at the World Cup, while William Saliba damaged his back. It would be no great surprise if Arsenal started the season slowly.

But who is equipped to take advantage? The previous two league title winners are under new management. Enzo Maresca – Guardiola’s replacement at Manchester City – is a curious manager in that his record is rather better than the experience of watching his teams play. Although his reputation was enhanced by Chelsea’s decline after his departure, it shouldn’t be forgotten just how frustrated Leicester and Chelsea fans became at times with the cautious nature of his football. Arne Slot showed at Liverpool that it is, at least in the short term, possible to thrive when following one of the big beasts but it remains an enormous challenge to succeed somebody who has defined the personality of a club.

Andoni Iraola impressed at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth, but the truth is that it’s impossible to know how anybody will adapt to the greater scrutiny of a club such as Liverpool, no matter how composed they may previously have appeared.

There’s a lingering doubt about his Bournemouth’s propensity to concede late goals. It may be that a deeper bench offers an immediate solution but equally that could indicate a problem with load management – and that is not going to be made any easier by involvement in the Champions League. Iraola has always relied on extremely physical training sessions, but they will have to be tempered, at least to an extent, by the demands of European football, in which Iraola has little experience.

Similar questions can be asked of Michael Carrick at Manchester United. He did enough last season that United effectively had to appoint him, without doing enough to offer overwhelming proof of his abilities. Signings so far seem to have addressed the right areas in the squad, but the big issue is whether he can handle the demands of playing in multiple competitions. United finished third last season without ever playing a team who had played fewer matches than them.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

So demanding is the modern calendar that fatigue may end up being a bigger factor than any manager. If you are a superclub, the key to having a bad season, as United have demonstrated, is to have one so bad that you don’t qualify for any form of European competition.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso endured an awkward few months at Real Madrid but has the time to impose his ideas at Chelsea. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters

Which is extremely good news for Chelsea. Not only do they have, in Xabi Alonso, one of Europe’s most promising young managers but he has time to impose his ideas and his side will be fresher than their opponents in almost every game this season.

Emery’s domination of the Europa League has paradoxically given him a reputation of not quite being of the highest tier, but if Aston Villa can find a way of winning games beyond Morgan Rogers thrashing long-range efforts into the top corner, he has a great opportunity to impose himself. De Zerbi, who has the charisma of a leading figure, should also find himself in the Champions League qualification shake-up given Tottenham’s summer signings and their lack of European football.

The big beasts may have gone but that simply means the Premier League is entering a new phase. What matters now is the battle to be the next alpha. Arteta is perhaps best placed, but the contenders are legion. The land awaits its next giant.

Sports.title: There can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removed | Nick Ames
Sports.content:
There is no time to dance around the subject. Gianni Infantino must stand down as Fifa president or otherwise be legally removed. No fresh chances can be made available for an official who has demolished trust in football’s integrity and governance, trashing all remaining credibility of the body that oversees the world’s most-cherished sport.

Infantino was forced into a humiliating climbdown on Saturday morning when he accepted the failure of his plan to sell off portions of the World Cup to private investment. He resolved to resume dialogue about football’s growth “in the spirit of shared interest in our game”. But such a naked attempt to save his own skin cannot hold. Every day Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor.

The overreach involved in unilaterally launching the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme – with its vision to place huge influence on football’s future in the palms of venture capitalists – would be enough to bring down most leaders. But Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond that. He has routinely made a mockery of Fifa’s own statutes and governance regulations, so nobody should be surprised that patience has finally snapped in corridors of power globally. Fifa’s “football unites the world” slogan has never looked more empty.

Article 10.3 of those regulations, which specifically pertains to the presidency, requires the incumbent to ensure “Fifa’s objectives, mission, strategic direction, policies and values are sustainably pursued, protected and implemented, and that a positive image of Fifa is fostered”. It stipulates “promoting friendly and peaceful relations within Fifa”, which is a nonsense given the degree to which federations and senior personnel have distanced themselves from Infantino in recent days.

The rules give no green light to the pursuit of multiple private projects that, most recently in lockstep with the current US administration or its tributaries, have been tabled with scant appetite for oversight or explanation.

Where to begin? The Folarin Balogun saga tipped many leading figures in football, particularly in Europe, towards the edge. There had already been widespread bafflement and disgust at Infantino’s presentation of the new Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump in December, with little background given about the process and highly contestable information provided about the US president’s qualifying achievements. Stakeholders were frustrated by a lack of consultation about the introduction of “hydration breaks”, which fundamentally toyed with the fabric of matches at this summer’s World Cup.

View image in fullscreen The saga involving Folarin Balogun after his ban for a red card was suspended tipped many leading figures in football towards the edge. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

The bizarre expedited bidding process for the 2034 tournament, which resulted in Saudi Arabia’s candidature being waved through in December 2024, also brought widespread criticism. This list only covers the past 20 months of controversies inflicted by Infantino, capped on Friday by revelations that plans for a 64-team World Cup are in full swing.

When a scathing statement from Uefa on Saturday called for an end to “secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game”, it was not only referring to the FFE project and its casual sidelining of other decision makers within Fifa.

A critical mass has been reached. Uefa took a decisive lead in following more than a year of harsh words with strong, united action in pledging to boycott future Fifa tournaments if Infantino did not withdraw his plan. It undoubtedly influenced the outcome and the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, secured an achievement that may define his own reign. But it will mean nothing if Infantino, who is understood to have deployed a major consultancy to smooth relations with federations in recent days, is given the oxygen to dangle fresh promises and turn heads back towards the status quo.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond attempting to launch the Fifa Forward Enterprise unilaterally. Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPA

There is an acknowledgment within Uefa and beyond that the pace must not let up. Senior figures are adamant Infantino must not survive the current scandal. Some insiders feel a crucial next step will be for member associations, the overwhelming majority of whom had formally pledged their support for Infantino’s re-election next March, to recall those letters.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Doing so requires a request to Fifa but could, in sufficient numbers, be a de facto vote of no confidence in Infantino. Fifa had lobbied aggressively for those submissions but many FAs would now be red faced if their expression of fealty towards Infantino was more widely publicised.

Member associations have a duty not to shrink in staving off existential threats to their sport otherwise they, like Infantino, are doing it an egregious disservice. Backing away now would mean leaving the job half done at best.

Uefa have pledged to devise a new method for distributing Fifa’s wealth, delving into its multibillion cash reserves without “selling the family silver”. Behind the scenes it continues to work with other confederations in an effort to find credible candidates for Infantino’s replacement, with a view to running in the election should the Swiss hold on until then. The present crisis can be used to reshape football for the better but only if Infantino is not in situ to impose the final say.

The alternative is that Fifa, and by extension the game, continue lurching from one disaster to the next. It is no laughing matter when the public conversation around football centres on one man, his ego and brazen ventures.

In December Zvonimir Boban, a former sidekick to Infantino as Fifa’s deputy secretary general, told the Guardian that “the way is lost” after the peace prize award to Trump. Fifa will not find a route back until Infantino plays no further part in its operation.

Sports.title: Faster, faster: Iraola in a rush to plug Liverpool gaps before Premier League starts
Sports.content:
“Faster, faster,” bellowed Andoni Iraola throughout the open training session Liverpool held in Chicago on Friday. His first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach ends at the city’s famous Soldier Field Stadium on Sunday, with a friendly against Leeds, and “faster, faster” could apply to all aspects of the club’s preparations for a new Premier League campaign that begins in three weeks’ time.

Iraola was in his element as he immersed himself at the centre of every training drill that Liverpool performed at Chicago Fire’s Endeavor Health Performance Center, their base for the past two weeks in the US. “Faster, faster” was the new head coach’s instruction to his players as three teams of seven worked on their pressing games. He also shouted it when they walked over to a different pitch, recently vacated by Robert Lewandowski and his new Chicago Fire teammates, to work on offensive and defensive set-piece routines. Sprints were demanded following every rondo.

There is an urgency to Iraola’s situation at Liverpool as he works towards his first season in charge, not only to his style of football. Post World-Cup holidays have deprived him of eight first-team players so far, injuries of a further six.

It was telling that, after Liverpool’s open training session had ended, many of the fans invited headed to the gym for a look through its glass windows. Jérémy Jacquet, Liverpool’s £60m recruit from Rennes, was inside working on his recovery from a shoulder problem.

He was joined by Giovanni Leoni, who is rehabilitating from an anterior cruciate ligament rupture and appears to have doubled in chest size since sustaining the injury on his Liverpool debut last September. Nearby was Joe Gomez, who pulled up with a muscle injury eight minutes into the first friendly of the tour. All central defenders, all out.

The concentration of problems in one particular area was a recurring theme under Arne Slot last season and has not eased yet. Two 18-year-olds, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, have impressed in their absence but Liverpool are looking to loan out the latter next season having been unable to secure a work permit.

Among the observers on Friday was Mike Gordon, the president of Liverpool’s owners, Fenway Sports Group, who has returned to a more hands-on role at the club after the departure of Michael Edwards as FSG’s chief executive of football.

View image in fullscreen Teenage defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is likely to be loaned out by Liverppool. Photograph: Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

Gordon is expected to be in attendance at Soldier Field on Sunday when Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak should feature for the first time in pre-season. FSG will not be the only ones at Liverpool looking for a return on their combined £241m investment in the pair.

“We need a very good version of Florian,” Iraola said this week, when confirming he intends to play the Germany international “in that position behind the striker” rather than on the left, where he operated without reward at the World Cup, or in the variety of roles that Slot tried without success.

Wirtz supplying Isak and/or Hugo Ekitiké was always the intended plan of attack for Liverpool last season. The trio ultimately played only 119 minutes together as injuries struck. That stat was never lost on Slot as he was ushered to the exit after a turbulent and toxic campaign.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool need a very good version of Isak, too. The excuse of playing catch-up having missed pre-season, or almost four months of the season due to a fractured ankle and fibula, no longer washes for a striker who featured in all four games of Sweden’s World Cup. Isak has looked sharp in pre-season training. He not only has to sustain that sharpness next season but convince he is a suitable fit for this Liverpool team.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz will be used behind the striker this season under Andoni Iraola for Liverpool. Photograph: Becky Oliver/LFC/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Iraola’s options and vision for Liverpool will improve as senior names return but he undoubtedly requires more help through the transfer market. Work is under way on a move for Bradley Barcola, who is open to leaving Paris Saint-Germain for Anfield, but a deal for a winger who the European champions value at £145m is yet to be struck.

A lack of defensive cover cost Liverpool last season and remains a glaring issue, and there are doubts over the futures of Curtis Jones, Federico Chiesa and Harvey Elliott, among others.

Liverpool’s head coach has admitted he “hates this month of August” because of the uncertainty that surrounds players while the season starts. “It’s difficult to build a proper team with a lot of question marks,” he added. Between Soldier Field on Sunday and St James’ Park on 23 August, the building work must accelerate.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Aberdeen’s late double stuns Hearts, St Johnstone edge thriller
Sports.content:
Hearts’ miserable summer continued as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1 to Aberdeen in their Premiership opener at Pittodrie.

Wouter Vrancken and Hearts looked on course for a much-needed victory after a turbulent few months as they led through Oisin McEntee’s first-half goal. But just as they looked to be closing out a first win at Pittodrie for more than a decade, Lewis Mayo equalised in the 90th minute before Kevin Nisbet won it for Aberdeen with a stoppage-time penalty after Stuart Findlay was sent off for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

It was a third consecutive defeat for Vrancken, who has endured a chastening start since replacing Derek McInnes in June. There were five changes to the side that lost Wednesday’s Champions League qualifier at home to Sturm Graz, with the goalkeeper Beau Reus and Laurent Mendy handed their debuts.

In what was their first league match since being pipped to the title by Celtic in May, the 1,600-strong travelling support could be regularly heard singing anti-SFA songs in protest at the contentious calls from officials in the closing matches of last season. There was also a sense of trepidation about the prospect of kicking off the new season at Pittodrie, where Hearts had not won in their previous 14 visits.

Hearts took the lead in the 35th minute after some pinball in the penalty area. Ba-Sy’s cutback from the left broke to Blair Spittal, whose shot was blocked by Nesta Guinness-Walker on the edge of the six-yard box. Dan Happe’s attempt to clear ran into the path of McEntee, who shot low into the net from seven yards.

Aberdeen levelled in the 90th minute when Mayo bundled in from close range after Happe headed Ronan’s free-kick back into the danger area. The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Toyosi Olusanya was hauled down by Findlay, who saw red, and Nisbet despatched the spot-kick.

Ibrahim Said netted a late winner as Motherwell started their league season as they left off by beating Hibernian at Easter Road. Said finished off an excellent counter-attack in the 85th minute to secure a 2-1 victory.

The Motherwell midfielder Oscar Priestman had earlier won and conceded a penalty. Lukas Fadinger put the visitors ahead five minutes before the end of a largely uneventful first half. Regan Charles-Cook missed a glorious chance to double the lead before Martin Boyle levelled in the 56th minute after being bundled over by Priestman.

Hibs had two efforts cleared off the line by Martin Moorman before Said slotted home his fourth goal for the club.

St Johnstone twice gave up the lead before storming back to edge a seven-goal thriller at home to Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Josh Fowler gave the home side a 16th-minute lead but Greg Kiltie equalised against the run of play. Cheick Diabate’s header put the home side back in front after 47 minutes but two quick goals from Joe Hugill and Jason Holt – into his own net – somehow saw the visitors lead.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Michael Schjønning-Larsen put through his own net and Kai Fotheringham grabbed a late winner.

“That was a test of character,” said Valakari, whose side came up as Championship winners last term. “Would we be this team who plays nice football in the Premiership but concedes goals and loses?”

The St Mirren manager, Craig McLeish, believes his team’s 2-0 win at Falkirk augurs well for a successful campaign.

McLeish is convinced his squad will improve on last season’s struggles before he steered Saints to safety when the interim head coach. He has set a high bar of the top six and a European qualification bid this term, and a double from Killian Phillips helped St Mirren get off to a fine start at Falkirk Stadium.

“I thought the performance was excellent and if we can build on that we can go and achieve something as a group,” McLeish said. “I’m delighted for the group. We got the result our performance deserved. I thought we were excellent.”

Sports.title: Robert Lewandowski strikes twice for Chicago Fire in MLS win over Charlotte
Sports.content:
Robert Lewandowski scored two goals on his home debut as the Chicago Fire eked out a 2-1 victory over Charlotte FC on ⁠Saturday. The win is Chicago’s first in Major League Soccer since the end of the international break.

Lewandowski, signed in late June as a free agent, produced a vintage performance to help the Fire (9-6-2, 29 points) close an ever-narrowing gap with the Eastern Conference’s top three clubs. Charlotte (7-7-4, 25pts) has now lost four of its last five road matches.

Pep ⁠Biel opened the scoring in the 18th minute for Charlotte. After playing a one-two with Idan ​Toklomati at the top of the box, ‌the Spanish attacker sped past his marker and ‌rifled his shot past Chicago goalkeeper Chris Brady into the top right corner. The goal was Biel’s ‌team-leading ninth of the season.

Lewandowski responded just two minutes later, scoring his first goal in a Chicago uniform. Jonathan Bamba lofted a through-ball to Philip Zinckernagel, who headed it to an incoming Lewandowski. After faking a shot, Lewandowski put the ball on his right foot and slotted into the bottom ‌left corner, past goalkeeper Kristijan Kahlina.

The Fire almost took the lead when Zinckernagel found Robin Lod open in the box. However, the Finnish midfielder couldn’t steer his shot on ​target at such a steep angle, and Lewandowski could not connect with the ball at the far post.

In the 56th minute, Lewandowski played a pinpoint through-ball to a streaking Zinckernagel, setting him ⁠up for a one-on-one with Kahlina. Zinckernagel took one too many touches ​as he neared the keeper, who deflected his tight-angle shot away.

Chicago found the go-ahead goal in the 68th minute ​when Andrew Gutman found Lod ‌just outside the ​box in transition. Lod ​played Lewandowski in with a through ball, and the former Dortmund, Bayern Munich and Barcelona striker beat Kahlina at close range for his second goal of the game.

Lionel Messi returned to MLS action on Saturday, coming on in the second half as his Inter Miami side drew 2-2 with Columbus Crew. The Argentina star could not mark his return with a goal, though, twice shooting wide.

View image in fullscreen Luis Suárez celebrates after opening the scoring for Inter Miami. Photograph: Marta Lavandier/AP

Luis Suárez scored his seventh goal in his last four games to put Miami 1-0 up in the 16th minute, but Casemiro scored an own goal to draw Columbus level. Suárez then set up Noah Allen to head the hosts back in fronts, but midfielder Brais Méndez levelled again with a late free-kick on his debut for the Crew.

Tai Baribo scored in the 77th minute to cap a second-half rally from two goals down as DC United earned ⁠a 2-2 home draw against Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sam Surridge’s penalty and Shakur Mohammed’s strike came eight minutes apart in the first half for Nashville, but Silvan Hefti volleyed in from a corner to make it 2-1 in the 56th minute. Baribo levelled for DC United when his shot from out wide beat Nashville keeper Brian Schwake.

Thomas Müller’s penalty secured a 1-1 draw for the Vancouver Whitecaps against LAFC on the team’s return to BC Place Stadium. Son Heung-min had fired the visitors ahead with a neat turn and shot, but Müller won and converted a 76th-minute spot-kick after he was hauled down in the box by defender Yevhen Cheberko.

Brandon Bye scored the winning goal in the 82nd minute as the Portland Timbers handed the Seattle Sounders their sixth straight loss. Kevin Kelsey also scored for the Timbers, who are undefeated in four games after this 2-1 win. Kalani Kossa-Rienzi scored for the Sounders, who are dealing with a spate of injuries.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.

The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.

“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.

Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.

Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also secured the France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.

Brentford seal record Sangaré deal

Brentford have signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joins Brentford on a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.

“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sangaré left Austria’s Rapid Vienna to ‌join Lens last year, and featured prominently as they won the ​French Cup for the first time and finished second in Ligue 1.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré has swapped RC Lens for Brentford in a £39m move. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

Bournemouth have announced the signing of António Silva from Benfica for a fee believed to be in the region of £25m. The 22-year-old defender becomes new manager Marco Rose’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Álvaro Rodríguez earlier this week.

Silva made 235 senior appearances for Benfica and collected six major honours during his time in Portugal. He told the club website: “I am very happy to be here. It’s a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League.

“The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans. We have everything here that helps us perform on the pitch, and I can’t wait to get started.”

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley consortium set to buy Gold family’s 25.1% stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reached an agreement to buy a ‌25.1% stake in West ⁠Ham after Vanessa Gold, daughter of the former chair David Gold, ⁠agreed to sell ⁠her ​family’s shares in the Championship club.

The move by the businesswoman who helped lead the Saudi consortium takeover of Newcastle comes after a previously agreed sale to fellow shareholder and Czech businessman ⁠Daniel Kretinsky fell through.

The Gold family ​trust owns the 25.1% stake in West Ham, ‌who were relegated from the Premier League last season just two seasons after winning the Europa Conference League in 2023. However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Gold said in a statement: “As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023. Whether as a youth team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father’s priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

“On June 12, Daniel Kretínsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

View image in fullscreen West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/Reuters

“In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium led by Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions. My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham. While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club’s best interests, as my father did and would expect of me.”



Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy-out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club’s rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on 16 August.

Sports.title: Charlie Austin reveals first coaching job rejection at former club
Sports.content:
Charlie Austin reveals first coaching job rejection at former club

Charlie Austin has revealed that he was rejected by his former club QPR after applying for a coaching job.

The 37-year-old striker posted the disappointing news on social media as he missed out on working within QPR's academy.

2 Austin has been rejected after an interview for an academy coaching job at QPR Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Austin, who played 148 times and scored 61 goals across three spells with the Championship side, had an interview for the position.

He posted on X: "First job interview disappointment.

"Gutted not to progress to the next stage for @QPRAcademy coaching team. The club I really wanted to work with.

"Will keep working hard and hoping my time will come.

"Good luck to whoever lands the role, what a club you get to join!"

In reply to his post, a fan questioned whether Austin expected to get the coaching role as he previously played for QPR.

However, he made sure to shut those suggestions down, adding: "No hidden agenda. Just honest disappointment at missing out on a role at a club I think highly of.

"Nothing but respect for QPR, the process was fair and professional, everyone was great.

"As I said will keep working hard for my time to come! This just weren’t my time."

Austin has not yet taken a role in coaching, and his playing career is still ongoing with semi-pro club Hungerford Town.

2 Austin is hoping to take his first steps into football coaching Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Austin's goal-filled career

Austin is clearly looking for the next step in his career as he nears the end of his playing days at the age of 37.

The forward has played 218 times in the Championship and over 100 times in the Premier League since 2011.

As mentioned, he played 148 times for QPR, while he has also featured 133 times for Swindon Town, scoring 60 goals.

He made 90 appearances for Burnley too, netting 44 times.

Austin scored 31 times across his time with Southampton and West Brom, and also had a stint in Australia in 2022.

In total across his professional playing career, he scored exactly 200 goals in 510 games across all levels.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League striker Victor Anichebe could buy fairytale EFL club
Sports.content:
Former Premier League striker Victor Anichebe is reportedly spearheading a bid to take over Bromley.

Anichebe is said to be leading talks to buy the newly-promoted League One club, amid their rise up the EFL.



2 Ex-Everton striker Anichebe is said to be leading talks over a potential takeover of Bromley Credit: Getty

Bromley have gone from the National League to the third tier of the English football pyramid in just two years.

Following promotion to League Two in 2024, they went on to get promoted to League One at the end of last season.

It's widely considered a fairytale story, as this will be their first ever campaign at this level - and now they could end up being taken over by an ex-Premier League star.



Anichebe is now locked in talks with Bromley owner Robin Stanton-Gleaves, according to The Sun. talkSPORT has contacted Bromley for comment.

The 38-year-old was also linked to a potential takeover of non-league side Gateshead last year.



But now, he could enter ownership at a higher level, with Bromley bosses said to understand that they need some extra cash to compete in League One.

It is reported that Anichebe is already having an impact on Bromley's summer recruitment ahead of a proposed takeover.



He is the owner of Lumira Group, who are 'a long-term holding company investing in sport, education, healthcare and infrastructure across the UK'.

The former Nigeria international was recently involved in a £20million proposal for a new leisure development in Liverpool.

And he could be closing in on becoming a football club owner for the first time as he spearheads his group in negotiations.

2 Bromley could be set to have an ex-Premier League star in charge of the club Credit: Getty



Bromley kickstart their 2026/27 campaign with a Carabao Cup first round tie against Reading on Saturday.

They then play their first ever League One match against Barnsley a week later on Saturday, August 15.

Anichebe's playing career

Anichebe has moved into the business side of sports since retiring from football in the summer of 2018.

But many fans will remember his days playing in the Premier League, where he made over 200 appearances.



He scored 27 goals and provided 12 assists across his spells with Everton, Sunderland and West Brom from 2006 to 2017.

The ex-forward spent the longest time at Everton, playing 168 times for the Toffees, scoring 26 goals in all competitions.

For West Brom, he netted nine times in 63 games, while for Sunderland, he scored three goals in 19 appearances.

On the international stage, Anichebe picked up 11 caps for Nigeria, scoring one goal for his country.

Sports.title: Vinicius Junior’s agency hit out at ‘fake and damaging’ reports in damning statement
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior’s agency hit out at ‘fake and damaging’ reports in damning statement

Vinicius Junior's agency, Roc Nation, has hit out at 'fake and damaging' reports from the media this summer.

Roc Nation Sports International released a damning statement on Sunday amid reports linking Vinicius Jr. to Arsenal.

3 Vini Jr.'s agency has released a damning statement regarding media reporting Credit: Getty

The statement called on journalists to be more 'accountable' and slammed 'unprofessional and uninformed' behaviour.

However, it did not specifically mention Vini Jr.'s transfer saga.

Roc Nation's president, Michael Yormark, posted on Instagram: "Roc Nation Sports International and our entire team cannot stand idle when unprofessional and uninformed media publish fake and damaging information for attention-seeking purposes.

"This is especially unacceptable when it personally targets our clients without any foundation.

"It is disruptive, harmful and libellous. Media outlets and journalists need to hold themselves more accountable."

Roc Nation are an agency, founded by legendary music artist Jay-Z, that represents multiple sports stars across the world.

They work with many NFL players, including Saquon Barkley, as well as NBA stars like Kyrie Irving and LaMelo Ball.

As well as Vini Jr, they also represent incoming Real signing Yan Diomande, Gabriel Martinelli and Endrick among other footballers.

Vinicius Junior to Arsenal latest

It's not clear whether Roc Nation are speaking about Vinicius Jr. and the ongoing rumours surrounding a Real Madrid exit.

But fans are sure to try and connect the two, with the Brazilian still being linked to Premier League champions Arsenal.

3 Roc Nation posted the statement titled 'Fake News' but didn't mention Vini Jr. Credit: Instagram @michaelyormark

Vini Jr. is out of contract at Real next year, and talkSPORT understands talks are still ongoing over him signing a new deal.

Whilst that stand-off continues, the Gunners are contemplating making a move for the superstar winger.

Club-to-club talks are not yet underway though, and Jose Mourinho is understood to want to keep Vini Jr. at the Bernabeu.

The saga is sure to rumble on as the transfer window remains open and his contract talks remain ongoing.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has even been asked about the links during the Gunners' pre-season campaign.

When asked, 'When's Vini joining?', Arteta smiled in reaction.

3 The Real Madrid superstar's contract runs out next summer and Arsenal are interested Credit: Getty

And he later said to reporters on whether he will be bringing in some more signings this summer: "Well, we are already active trying to improve and evolve the team – that's clear.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else, and you can just see the transfer market and our opponents what we are doing.

"We won't sit still and we are very ambitious what we want to do."

Sports.title: Chelsea complete signing of World Cup star on seven-year deal
Sports.content:
Valentin Barco has signed a seven-year contract at Chelsea to join from sister club Strasbourg.

The 22-year-old, who used to ply his trade at Brighton, completes his move to the Blues with the deal being agreed ahead of the summer.



2 Barco brings some Premier League experience on his return to England Credit: Getty

He initially signed for Strasbourg on loan from Brighton in February 2025, before completing a switch worth £8million in July of that year.

Barco made seven appearances for the Seagulls ahead of his transfer to France, where he worked under former Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior.

Chelsea have opted to press ahead with the deal despite Rosenior being sacked from his post.



Barco was part of Argentina's World Cup squad this summer, playing in their group stage victory over Jordan.

But as a midfielder, he could face plenty of competition at Stamford Bridge when he arrives later this year.



Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez, Romeo Lavia and Dario Essugo are midfield options at the disposal of new manager Xabi Alonso.

However, Barco could have one less competitor amid the uncertainty over Fernandez and his future in west London.



Barco in, Fernandez out?

After Chelsea were thrashed 8-2 on aggregate by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League in March, Fernandez criticised the club's board.

He said he didn't understand their decision to allow head coach Enzo Maresca to leave the club at the beginning of the year.

Fernandez then generated speculation over a move to Real Madrid as he admitted he would like to live in the Spanish capital.

2 Barco could end up replacing Fernandez should he leave the club Credit: Getty



talkSPORT understands he is open to a move to Madrid this summer, although the Spanish giants publicly denied their interest in Fernandez in July.

Fernandez was subsequently sanctioned for the comments having been prevented from playing Chelsea's FA Cup win over Port Vale in April, which finished 7-0 to Chelsea.

He was also not involved in their Premier League fixture away at Manchester City on April 12 as well.

Busy summer

Barco is the latest addition for Chelsea, which has seen them splash out on numerous summer signings.



They broke the transfer record for a British player with the £117million acquisition of England star Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Meanwhile, France centre-back Maxence Lacroix has joined in a £52m deal from Crystal Palace.

The Blues announced the signing of former Arsenal and Manchester United striker Danny Welbeck on a two-year deal.

And former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson is set to complete his move to the west London club imminently.

Sports.title: Liverpool could make shock Curtis Jones U-turn despite on-field bust up with Dominik Szoboszlai
Sports.content:
Liverpool could make shock Curtis Jones U-turn despite on-field bust up with Dominik Szoboszlai

Liverpool may yet offer Curtis Jones a new contract at the club.

That's despite the midfielder's spat with teammate Dominik Szoboszlai.

2 Jones argued with Szoboszlai, seemingly upset at not being handed the captain's armband after the Hungarian was substituted against Wrexham Credit: X / @anythingLFC_

The pair clashed following Liverpool's pre-season win over Wrexham in New York, with fellow Reds players Kostas Tsimikas and Jeremie Frimpong stepping in to try and diffuse the situation.

Inter Milan are among the clubs interested in signing Jones but Liverpool are not dead set on offloading their academy graduate, reports Ben Jacobs.

Joining Shaun Custis and Henry Winter on talkSPORT, Jacobs explained: "Inter are pushing for Curtis Jones. They made an offer, in inverted commas – although Liverpool don’t really see it as a formal bid – in the region of €35million (approximately £29m) and that’s their third approach – €32million and €25million were the other numbers.

"And Jones would welcome a move to Inter. Liverpool want a minimum of €40m and in this inflated market, some people are even saying €50m.

"And yet, if the window shuts, we might get the opposite extreme, because Andoni Iraola’s said that he likes Curtis Jones – and despite the bust-up you mentioned, Liverpool are not averse to offering Jones a new deal if he stays.

"But my sense is Inter will be back and Liverpool are a bit frustrated by this because they don’t want it through intermediaries anymore.

"The perspective of the club, according to my info, is if Inter want Curtis Jones – a bit like Bruno Guimaraes, Newcastle-Arsenal – knock on our front door, make us a formal offer and then you might find a financial compromise.

"So, this is going to be one to watch in the month of August."

Jones has just under a year to run on his Liverpool contract, meaning he would be available on a free transfer next summer should he not sign an extension – a situation the Reds will want to avoid.

The six-cap England international has made over 200 appearances for his boyhood club since making his first-team debut shortly before his 18th birthday in January 2019.

2 Jones scored on his England debut against Greece in 2024 Credit: AFP

A two-time Premier League champion, Jones featured 49 times for Liverpool in all competitions last season.

But the incident with Szboszlai has not reflected well on the former European U-21 champion.

Peterborough owner and Liverpool fan Darragh MacAnthony blasted Jones on talkSPORT, saying on Thursday: "He's acting like a spoilt brat.

"I saw his behaviour last night on the pitch... I understand the frustration that he should have got the armband. He's a Scouser; he's been there 20 years, blah blah blah.

"But to act like that and to carry it on, because it went on for about two minutes.

"He was having a go at Szoboszlai, who handed the armband over, I think, to Tsimikas, I believe Curtis Jones had the temper tantrum over that.

"That behaviour can't happen, not from a graduate from the academy; he's too into himself."

Sports.title: ‘Not that good’ – Hansi Flick offers blunt verdict on new Barcelona star’s first appearance in Birmingham friendly
Sports.content:
‘Not that good’ – Hansi Flick offers blunt verdict on new Barcelona star’s first appearance in Birmingham friendly

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick was not overly impressed with Karim Adeyemi on his debut for the club against Birmingham.

Adeyemi joined Barca from Borussia Dortmund at the start of July, waiting a month to make his first appearance.

2 Adeyemi made his Barcelona debut in their friendly loss to Birmingham Credit: Getty

He started for the Spanish giants against Championship side Birmingham during their match on Friday evening, which saw Barcelona lose on penalties after playing out a 2-2 draw.

However, the German winger was substituted at half time, along with three other of his new teammates.

During his first 45 minutes as a Barca player, Adeyemi had one shot at goal, which was blocked in the opening stages.

He completed 76 per cent of his passes, but failed to complete a dribble and lost possession nine times in total.

His manager, Flick, then admitted that he was not very impressed with his compatriot's performance on his debut.

"Karim, some things he did were not that good," he said post-match.

Although Flick did add: "I think he has more potential to show, but he is still in the first week of training, so that's normal.

"I've seen a better Karim in training with his speed and finishing, but he has a lot of potential and can give us a lot.”

Of course, after just 45 minutes of action, Adeyemi retains the belief of his boss, but it seems he's getting some tough love.

Flick opted not to try and sign Manchester United's Marcus Rashford on a permanent deal this summer, getting Adeyemi in instead.

2 Adeyemi lost the ball nine times in his 45-minute first appearance for Barca Credit: Getty

Adeyemi's next outing

Adeyemi will have another chance to make his mark at Barcelona in their next pre-season friendlies on August 8.

Barca take on Nottingham Forest and Udinese on the same day, with both games being played in Italy.

He would have had another game in England after taking on Birmingham, but a scheduled match against Preston North End was cancelled on Sunday.

Flick's men are set to travel back to Spain at the start of the week before their next friendlies in Italy.

Barcelona's first LaLiga game of the season is against Elche on August 23, after another pre-season match against Egyptian side Al Ahly.

Adeyemi will hope to make a similar impact to Rashford, who provided 14 goals and 14 assists in 49 appearances last season.

For Dortmund last term, Adeyemi scored ten goals and provided seven assists across 39 games in all competitions.

Sports.title: Liam Delap has two Premier League options following Danny Welbeck’s move to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Liam Delap has two Premier League options following Danny Welbeck’s move to Chelsea

Danny Welbeck's arrival at Chelsea has thrown Liam Delap's Stamford Bridge future into fresh doubt.

Welbeck completed a surprise move from Brighton on Saturday, increasing competition for places up front with the Blues.



2 The 35-year-old has penned a two-year deal with Chelsea Credit: Getty

And Delap may be one of a number of Chelsea players having to look elsewhere in search of regular football, as talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs told Shaun Custis and Henry Winter.

Noting how fellow Blues striker Nicolas Jackson has been linked with a move to Aston Villa, Jacobs said: “And I think there’s a fair chance that Liam Delap goes, and there’s certainly historical interest from both Everton and Newcastle and growing Premier League interest more generally.

“And the thing about both Delap and Jackson is that they have to understand are they equal with Welbeck or are they effectively number three and different kind of profiles? Or are they lower down?



“And if they’re lower down, you can say you want to fight for your place, but with only domestic football, they’ll realise very quickly that they have to go.

“So, departures are going to be key there.”

Delap joined Chelsea from Ipswich last summer when the Blues activated his £30million release clause.



And the 23-year-old son of Premier League cult hero Rory Delap went on to make 41 appearances for the Blues in all competitions.

However, he only managed two goals and Chelsea have made further centre forward additions this summer.



As well as Welbeck, the Blues have signed Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg – though the Netherlands international could already be on his way out of Stamford Bridge, albeit not permanently.

Delap scored 12 goals in 2024/25, Ipswich's first campaign back in the top flight, so he has shown he can cut it at this level and that he could be a very handy addition for another club.

2 Delap only scored one Premier League goal in his first season at Chelsea Credit: Getty

He must also have his international career in mind, having represented England up to under-21 level. Delap has yet to be called up to the Three Lions senior squad, however.



He is also eligible to play for the Republic of Ireland through his ancestry, with his father earning 11 caps for the country.

Chelsea continued their preparations for the new season with a dramatic 2-1 defeat to ten-man Tottenham in Sydney on Saturday.

Delap was involved but only as a late substitute.

The Blues begin the 2026/27 Premier League campaign, under new manager Xabi Alonso, away to local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Sports.title: Barcelona ‘forced to scrap pre-season friendly’ against EFL side just a day before game
Sports.content:
Barcelona ‘forced to scrap pre-season friendly’ against EFL side just a day before game

Barcelona's scheduled friendly against Preston North End has been scrapped just a day before it was due to take place.

The Spanish giants, who took on Birmingham City last week, were set to face Championship side Preston on Monday.

3 Barcelona's pre-season in England has been cut short after the cancellation Credit: Getty

But the behind-closed-doors match will no longer be going ahead, as Barca have pulled out of the game due to a bizarre reason.

According to Spanish outlet Sport, they have cancelled the fixture as Preston did not have enough available first-team players.

The Lilywhites are said to have offered to field an U21 outfit instead, but Barca refused and opted to scrap the game entirely.

Preston are reported to have not wanted to risk any of their key players in the friendly with the season starting next week.

They take on Huddersfield in the Carabao Cup on August 8.

Barcelona would have been taking on the EFL club at St George's Park, with kick-off set for Monday morning.

But instead, they're going to have a training session.

And Hansi Flick's side are also said to now be flying back to Spain earlier than scheduled due to the cancellation.

Barcelona's pre-season so far

Flick and his squad have been in England for their season preparations, coming up against Birmingham on Friday.

Barca were beaten 3-2 on penalties by Chris Davies' Blues after a 2-2 draw in normal time at St. Andrews.

3 Flick and his squad are going to train in England rather than play Preston's B-team Credit: Getty

Real Madrid and England superstar Jude Bellingham watched on from the stands as his club rivals lost.

Their only other pre-season clash so far came against lower-league Spanish side Europa, beating them 4-1.

Next up for the reigning La Liga champions will be Nottingham Forest on August 8, while another XI take on Udinese on the same day and they then face Al Ahli on August 19.

Preston focusing on season opener

As for Preston, they are clearly putting all of their focus on their first competitive game of the season next week.

Rather than using first-team players against Barcelona, they wanted to keep their key stars fit for the campaign.

Paul Heckingbottom's men take on Huddersfield in the first round of the Carabao Cup on August 8 at 3pm.

3 Preston and Heckingbottom don't want to risk first-team players against Barca Credit: Getty

They then start the Championship season with a trip to newly-promoted Bolton a week later on August 15.

Sports.title: Argentinian star signs for Chelsea, Newcastle's £27m goalkeeping target completes medical, Bournemouth bag Sevilla ace - while Hull are set to beat Rangers and Cardiff City to highly-rated Norwegian: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Argentinian star signs for Chelsea, Newcastle's £27m goalkeeping target completes medical, Bournemouth bag Sevilla ace - while Hull are set to beat Rangers and Cardiff City to highly-rated Norwegian: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Blues sign England nemesis

Chelsea have completed the signing of Argentina midfielder Valentin Barco from sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year contract.

The 22-year-old stirred controversy when his over-zealous celebrations of Argentina's victory over England at the World Cup provoked an angry reaction from Jude Bellingham.

Barco, who previously made six Premier League appearances for Brighton, has been signed following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid earlier this summer but he has been playing in midfield.

As Daily Mail Sport reported in May, he left for Chelsea at the end of the season, saying his farewells to Strasbourg supporters.

Chelsea are also continuing negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Chelsea have completed the signing of England World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco (right)

Tractor Boys close in on new midfielder

Ipswich Town are closing in on the £16million signing of Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, the Portuguese midfielder was leaning towards a move to Portman Road after they declared their interest even though Hull City had been in advanced talks over an initial loan for the 26-year-old.

However, Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic revealed over the weekend that they were set to miss out to a club that was willing to sign him on a permanent deal.

Spurs target Liverpool star

Tottenham have made their interest known in Cody Gakpo but Liverpool have no plans to sell.

Liverpool, who continue to work on a deal for Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola, are looking to add attacking quality rather than lose it. Gakpo, 27, is one year in to a new long-term contract and with current market prices escalating for players of his experience, it would take a huge sum to change Liverpool's stance.

Tottenham are also keeping a watching brief on Omar Marmoush at Manchester City as well as negotiating for Savinho.

Elsewhere, Cologne have asked to take Tottenham winger Mikey Moore on loan.

The 18-year-old has a number of options including an offer to return on loan to Rangers.

Newcastle's new No 1 completes medical ahead of transfer

Goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek has completed his Newcastle United medical in Spain, and is set to be announced as the club’s latest signing.

Newcastle activated his £25.7m release clause and the player travelled to La Manga on Saturday.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, the 24-year-old Czech is being brought in as the club’s new first-choice option in goal.

Lukas Hornicek has completed his medical ahead of joining Newcastle in a £25.7million deal

Bournemouth bolster full-back options

Bournemouth have agreed an £11.2m deal with Sevilla for right-back Juanlu Sanchez.

The deal is worth £9.5m plus a potential £1.7m in add-ons while Sevilla retain a 10 per sell-on.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday, Bournemouth accelerated talks as they needed a right-back after the departure of Alex Jimenez to Fiorentina.

The 22-year-old Juanlu is a Spain international with four caps and had interest from Everton.

Wigan chasing Chelsea starlet

Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh is wanted on loan at Wigan Athletic.

The two clubs recently did business together when Chelsea completed the transfer of highly-rated 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Bettoni from Wigan on a four year contract.

Walsh became Chelsea’s youngest player to feature in the Champions League last season and will be hoping to build on his senior breakthrough during the 2026-27 campaign.

He figured briefly in the friendly defeat to Spurs in the Sydney Cup and was among several academy players involved as Xabi Alonso took charge of his first training session, alongside senior players such as Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

Walsh has returned to pre-season looking physically bigger and stronger so Chelsea are keen to see how he copes with more competitive game time.

Hammers chase former Spurs star

West Ham have joined the clubs showing interest in AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott.

Como, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis have already made enquiries.

The former Tottenham academy graduate is in demand after scoring 31 goals last season.

Alkmaar though are reluctant to sell the 24-year-old Republic of Ireland international to a rival Dutch club.

West Ham have entered the race to sign former Tottenham forward Troy Parrott

Hull lead race for Norwegian star

Hull City are ready to fend off interest from Rangers and Cardiff City to sign highly-rated Norwegian midfielder Jens Hjerto-Dahl.

Cardiff had offered a club record fee for the 20-year-old from Tromso but Hull are offering him the chance to play in the Premier League.

The 6ft 4ins defensive midfielder has captained Norway at youth level and is an U21 international.

Hull are also advancing in talks for 18-year-old centre back Lucas Herrington from Colorado Rapids and winger Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.
