Sports.title: Glasgow has shown the Commonwealth Games are worth fighting for - now they MUST come back on free-to-air TV, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
Anyone who claims the Commonwealth Games mean nothing should speak to the crowd that gathered outside my hotel at 1am on Friday.

‘Let’s go to Maccies!’ bellowed a late-night reveller. I looked out the window and it was Emily Campbell, hours after winning gold in the weightlifting, leading a group of athletes and supporters on a night out in Glasgow.

One of the best things about these games, not by design, is how close the locals have been able to get to the competitors. One cost-cutting decision was to sacrifice the athletes’ village, meaning competitors have been scattered in hotels across the city.

It has been impossible to miss the tracksuits of 74 different nations that have descended upon Scotland for the past 11 days of competition. The fans have never felt closer.

Josh Kerr went for a jog along the river before winning gold in the mile. Duncan Scott fuelled up for the pool with a hefty breakfast at a cafe on Wilson Street. Even Adam Ramsay-Peaty had to catch the bus.

One downside of these games has been the lack of visibility to the casual sports fan. For the first time in 72 years, the BBC pulled out as the official broadcaster. TNT Sports has provided comprehensive coverage but the events have not cut through to the UK’s mainstream audience.

The Glasgow Commonwealth Games have been a huge success over the past week-and-a-half

The absence of household names like Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson is a blow though

Given the absence of household names such as Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, this competition does not have the clout to pull in subscribers. Joe Public will not go out of his way to find the bowls or an obscure judo bout.

How many people would have tuned in to watch Matt Weston win his Winter Olympics gold medals in Italy, if the skeleton had not been broadcast live on the BBC? Not many.

These Games have been packed with feel-good stories. They have offered the perfect antidote to the grubby boardroom battles at FIFA HQ, where Gianni Infantino has been trying to make a quick buck from selling the World Cup to the highest bidder.

With more exposure, the likes of Cyrille Tchatchet would have been front of the queue to sit on the One Show sofa this week. He overcame homelessness to win weightlifting silver for England, but will now return to the gym to train in relative obscurity.

This event is ripe for free-to-air TV — particularly if most of the superstars stay away — and a new UK broadcast arrangement must be top of the agenda for the 2030 edition in India.

‘The BBC has been a fantastic partner for a very long period, and we do have a relationship with them for this games,’ said Katie Sadleir, chief executive officer of the Commonwealth Games Federation. ‘We are doing BBC Radio, so they are involved.

‘We are thrilled with TNT and Warner Bros. Discovery [TNT’s parent company]. For £4.99 for 600 hours compared to 200 hours in Birmingham [who hosted the Games in 2022], we are very pleased with that relationship.

‘We are moving towards a much wider feel about how people consume the games. I look after the Commonwealth movement of 74 countries, and it is my responsibility to look globally in terms of viewership.

‘It’s a process we will work through with the organising committee in terms of who the broadcaster is for 2030. The BBC will definitely be part of that mix.’

This event was almost abandoned when Victoria pulled out as hosts three years ago.

Australia’s richest person, mining magnate Gina Rinehart, has been offering cash bonuses for her country’s podium finishers, ensuring they arrived with a packed squad and walked away on top of the medal count. Channel 7’s coverage reached 11.39 million in Down Under. Australia’s credibility will be damaged if they bid for future sporting events. Perhaps Rinehart should have stepped in sooner?

But Glasgow saved the day. Yes, there have been some empty seats, but the big-ticket events have sold out. They have not spent taxpayer money and their fit-for-purpose model could provide a blueprint for hosting events during days of economic uncertainty.

The athletes are closer to stars than ever before and there has been a buzz around the city (pictured - Scotland's Josh after winning the Men's One Mile final)

After uncertainty about the event, Glasgow saved the day and proved to be brilliant hosts

India have promised to supersize things for Ahmedabad 2030. They hope to sell out the world’s largest stadium and use the event to showcase their credentials as Olympic hosts.

Proposals have been made to turn the Commonwealths into a qualifying event for World Championships. But unless the Games can lure back all of the biggest names of track and field, the Glasgow model — backed up by terrestrial TV — may well be the future.

For now, it looks more like a launchpad for young Olympic hopefuls. Filip Nowacki and Amalie Smith have emerged as Team GB prospects in the pool, Henry Hobbs won gold on the bike and Emily Newnham showed promise on the track.

‘It’s an incredible opportunity for a lot of athletes,’ said Ramsay-Peaty. ‘It is a stepping stone to give a platform two years out from an Olympics. That’s why we have got to nurture it.’

The games have been reset and reimagined. The Glaswegian hosts have cut their cloth and done so with a smile.

‘People are talking about these Games on the streets,’ added Sadleir. ‘Everyone is going away buzzed about what happened and what they think the future is for the Commonwealth Sport movement.’

Sports.title: Boxer in 'critical but stable' condition after being rushed to hospital following sickening knockout as promoter Frank Warren issues statement
Sports.content:
Boxer Lee Reeves is 'critical but stable' having been hospitalised after being knocked out during his defeat by Gary Cully on Saturday night.

In what proved to be an enthralling all-Republic of Ireland bout, Reeves was stopped in the 10th and final round by Cully - who sent him tumbling to the canvas with a huge left hand.

There was immediate concern from those inside the 3Arena in Dublin as Reeves stayed down for several moments as officials and medical staff quickly came to his aid.

The 31-year-old was given some oxygen before he left the venue being carried off on a stretcher and taken to hospital.

A spokesperson from Queensberry Promotions said on Sunday evening: 'Lee Reeves is still in hospital, in a critical but stable condition.

'We will know more in the coming days, and our thoughts and prayers remain with Lee and his family.'

Lee Reeves (right) was rushed to hospital after being knocked out by Gary Cully on Saturday

Reeves was immeadiately attended to by after being stopped in the 10th round of his defeat - he is now 'stable but critical'

Taking to X to provide an update, Queensberry promoter Frank Warren had previously written: 'All our thoughts and prayers are with Lee Reeves and his family at this time as he remains in hospital.

'Everyone at Queensberry is thinking of him and we're in constant contact with his team regarding his condition as we hope for positive news.'

Victory for Cully meant he claimed the BUI Celtic super-lightweight title but despite the victory, his thoughts were with Reeves.

'My prayers and thoughts are with Lee Reeves, hopefully he's okay,' said a concerned Cully.

'He came in there as a big underdog after fighting relatively at a lower level up until now, but he really showed that he can operate at a higher level. Huge credit to him.'

Sports.title: Robert Lewandowski makes perfect start to MLS life with Chicago Fire as city lands the star attraction they have so desperately craved after missing out on Neymar, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Robert Lewandowski makes perfect start to MLS life with Chicago Fire as city lands the star attraction they have so desperately craved after missing out on Neymar, writes LEWIS STEELE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chicago prides itself on being one of the sporting capitals of the world.

It was the setting for the legendary era of Michael Jordan, Scottie Pippen and Dennis Rodman as part of the Chicago Bulls’ six NBA titles in the 1990s, as seen in The Last Dance docu-series on Netflix which many watched in the Covid-19 pandemic.

There is the Bears NFL team and, across the city, Wrigley Field is one of Major League Baseball’s most iconic stadiums and home to the Cubs, city rivals of the White Sox. The ice hockey team, the Blackhawks, often get big crowds.

Lagging somewhat behind, although certainly on the rise now, is the local football team. Fandom for Chicago Fire is spreading across the city at a rate not too much slower than the great fire of 1871 which the team – and the hit US television show – takes its name.

The reason? One of the greatest strikers of his generation in Robert Lewandowski, with a helping hand from a lesser-known Englishman pulling the strings.

Daily Mail Sport was in situ at Soldier Field as the big Polishman opened his account for his new team, signing on the back of winning 10 German Bundesligas (two with Borussia Dortmund, eight with Bayern Munich), a Champions League and three La Liga titles with Barcelona.

A home debut brace and the game-winner ✌️🔥



Robert Lewandowski's first match in Chicago is one to remember. pic.twitter.com/pt567KCnn0 — Major League Soccer (@MLS) August 2, 2026

Robert Lewandowski scored twice for Chicago Fire on his home MLS debut following his summer move from Barcelona

The man who brought him to Major League Soccer (MLS) is a 50-year-old born in Bedford, who has also held jobs as academy manager for Luton, Norwich and one of Europe’s success stories in Norwegian side Bodo/Glimt, who beat Manchester City, Atletico Madrid and Inter this year.

Gregg Broughton, who joined as sporting director after doing the same role at Blackburn, tells Daily Mail Sport on Lewandowski: ‘Robert had been somebody the club had their eyes on for a long time. We understand how MLS works. There is a huge Polish community here in Chicago.

‘We tried to sign Neymar in January 2025, we could not get that done but he shared an agent with Lewandowski. We knew he would have his pick of clubs in Europe, in Saudi Arabia and he might have done another year at Barca. We had to make Chicago Fire his choice.

‘So our head coach Gregg Berhalter (formerly of the US national team) went to Barcelona, Robert’s wife came here for a business trip so we took her out. We sent a private jet to Barca to pick him and his representatives up, bring them here and show them the city.

‘He knows what world-class looks like, he is alongside Messi and Ronaldo, he is perfect for us. Robert is humble, easy to get on with, drives standards every day, won’t accept things being anything except everyone giving their best at every moment.’

Lewandowski’s record speaks for itself: 41 goals in 82 Lech Poznan games, 103 in 187 for Dortmund, 344 in 375 for Bayern, 120 in 193 for Barca. In 2020, he scored 55 in 47, won the Champions League and was arguably robbed of a Ballon d’Or, it being canned due to Covid.

He scored twice on his home debut on Saturday as Fire beat Charlotte FC 2-1, a team managed by ex-Aston Villa, Brentford and Leicester boss Dean Smith with several other Englishmen including midfielder Ashley Westwood, once of Villa, Burnley and Crewe Alexandra.

The 37-year-old is clearly the star attraction. Just as sport atheists would flock to watch Jordan in the 1990s, there are Lewandowski shirts across the city and a huge influx of Polish fans at Soldier Field stadium, which made for a raucous atmosphere not associated with MLS.

The forward is a mega star and the United States side worked hard to bring him to the club

‘I’m really happy to be here,’ said Lewandowski. ‘I enjoy every day: the lifestyle, the club and the organisation. Everything is really at a top level. I cannot say one bad word about the club, and I’m very impressed that everything is working very well, both on and off the pitch.’

The state-of-the-art facilities are part of the sales pitch to future transfer targets and a big reason why Chicago Fire allow teams to train at their base – Manchester United and Liverpool have done so, while Germany recently used it as their World Cup camp.

Those at the club believe seeing their base can plant a seed of thought in players’ minds ahead of a future move to MLS. Club staffers joked to Daily Mail Sport this week that it was a shame Virgil van Dijk is not on this pre-season tour for Liverpool, given his deal is up next summer.

‘Chicago is an incredible city,’ adds Broughton. ‘The training ground is incredible and that is allowing us to build a world-class club, we are building a new stadium. American sport accepts you can take five years to rebuild a squad, in Europe you don’t have that time.

‘I want to achieve on-field success and the bigger picture is I want to build upon the footprint of the World Cup and Club World Cup here in America. Twenty years ago, you never saw football shirts here – now, down by the river, they’re everywhere.

‘But we want them to be Chicago Fire shirts. This city stops to talk about sport. When the Bears got to the play-offs, the queues just to get into bars were crazy, you can’t get a ticket for love nor money. We know football can do that and the plan is to get Fire to be part of that.’

Lewandowski can certainly help.

Sports.title: England's World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco joins Chelsea: Argentina star who provoked Three Lions in semi-final defeat confirms switch to Stamford Bridge after Atlanta antics
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.

Barco, 22, who can play in midfield and at left-back, joins the Blues from their sister club Strasbourg.

The Argentine hit the headlines last month when he clashed with Jude Bellingham after England's semi-final defeat at the World Cup.

Barco made just one substitute appearance at the tournament, but he infuriated the Three Lions after he sprinted across the pitch when Enzo Fernandez equalised late on in the clash.

He ran right in front of several England players and appeared to taunt them, before John Stones reacted by giving him a shove.

Barco later also came onto the pitch in the aftermath of Lautaro Martinez's winning goal.

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal

Barco clashed with Jude Bellingham after Argentina's semi-final victory over England

There were also reports that the new Chelsea star had been winding up the England bench for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

In response to his antics, Bellingham gave the 22-year-old a slap on the back of the head after the full-time whistle as Argentina's players celebrated, causing a scuffle on the pitch.

Given his involvement in the World Cup, Barco won't join up with his new team-mates until later in pre-season.

The versatile star began his career back home with Boca Juniors, making his debut at the age of 16.

After impressing in Argentina, Barco joined Brighton in 2024 for £7.4million yet he struggled to establish himself on the south coast, and spent time on loan at Sevilla and Strasbourg.

He joined Strasbourg permanently in July 2025 and was regularly linked with a move away after impressing in France, where his side qualified for Europe.

Barco contributed 12 goals and assists last season and his strong form saw him earn a place in Argentina's World Cup squad, although he played just 19 minutes in a group stage victory over Jordan.

Bellingham slapped Barco on the back of the head following his overzealous celebrations

His arrival at Stamford Bridge comes following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid, although Chelsea are still in negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Barco is the Blues' seventh signing of the summer, with Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra and former Strasbourg striker Emmanuel Emegha all also joining the club.

He has similarly become the 13th player to move between the French side and Chelsea since BlueCo took over Strasbourg in 2023, a year after they purchased the Premier League side.

Sports.title: Argentina's Valentin Barco earned a slap from Jude Bellingham and will feel the heat from English fans when he kicks off his Chelsea career... but here's how his talent can win over his petulance
Sports.content:
Argentina's Valentin Barco earned a slap from Jude Bellingham and will feel the heat from English fans when he kicks off his Chelsea career... but here's how his talent can win over his petulance

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It has been just over a fortnight since Argentina beat England in their World Cup semi-final grudge match, and it is fair to say the English are still feeling the heartache.

The pain of a late defeat was exacerbated by the taunting nature of the Argentine celebrations, as were several displays of clear aggression and petulance from the Albiceleste during their late reprise and eventual victory in Atlanta.

Perhaps one of the more memorable aspects of this provocative Argentine behaviour were the actions of Chelsea-bound Valentin Barco, whose move to Stamford Bridge was confirmed on Sunday evening.

The Blues’ latest acquisition, 22, will expect a hostile welcome to the Premier League by the vast majority of fans as a result of his antics in the semi-final.

Despite not playing in the match, the former Strasbourg man was unsportsmanlike to say the least in his celebration of Enzo Fernandez’s late equaliser, resulting in a bust-up with Three Lions hero Jude Bellingham, who slapped him on the back of the head after the game.

Jude Bellingham clashed with unused Argentina substitute Valentin Barco

Barco's provocative celebrations irked England's star man after their semi final clash

Bellingham delivered a slap on the back of the head for the defender, who is set to join Chelsea

Barco started this by bounding across the pitch and through a number of dejected English players after Fernandez’s effort flew past Jordan Pickford, with the substitute having no acceptable reason for being so far on the field of play.

While Barco clearly succeeded in his attempts to rattle Tuchel’s team, he may not have thought through the possible consequences.

Bellingham's relatively tame slap will most likely not be the final punishment the youngsterwill receive. With Barco joining Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in Ligue 1, one would imagine there may be some awkwardness with his new skipper Reece James and Chelsea's other English stars.

Perhaps, though, they will put it all to one side as they band together ahead of the new Premier League season. If so, the Argentine’s biggest concern should be the reception he can expect from opposing fans, as well as perhaps other members of the doomed England team.

Barco will, of course, have the opportunity to silence his critics with his ability on the pitch. The young man can look to the example set by outgoing Chelsea star Marc Cucurella, who was in a similar position to the full-back just two years ago.

Off the back of Euro 2024 final, when his Spain side beat England 2-1, the left back was the subject of major derision and hatred from the English press and supporters alike due to his antics during the game and in the post-match celebrations.

Cucurella himself said he thought he was being treated more harshly by the authorities, saying they were 'going after' him as 'they're hurt'.

However, two years later he leaves England for Real Madrid having earned respect through his excellent performances at Stamford Bridge.

But matching the Spaniard’s trajectory will not be easy for Barco, partly because the Boca Juniors academy graduate has failed to impress before in the Premier League, during his stint at Brighton.

Barco featured as a substitute in the group-stage win over Jordan but did not play in any of Argentina's other seven matches at the World Cup

His underwhelming performances on the south coast were characterised mainly by an inability to deal with the pace and physicality of the division, a common obstacle for foreign imports in the Premier League. But what was more worrying was the surprisingly small amount of quality he displayed on the ball, as ever since he first gained attention from European clubs at a very young age he has always been viewed as extremely technically gifted.

However, in spite of this disappointing spell at Brighton, he found his footing in France and quickly became a key figure in Liam Rosenior’s 2024-25 Strasbourg side.

In Ligue 1, the Argentinian regained confidence and enjoyed a great run of form in the season just gone under Liam Rosenior and eventually Gary O’Neil, which ultimately earned him a place in Lionel Scaloni’s 2026 World Cup squad. Barco played an impressive 43 games for Strasbourg in all competitions last season, registering three goals and six assists.

Barco has joined Chelsea after making a name for himself for all the wrong reasons

As a result, Barco has become the latest Strasbourg player to have earned a move from North France to West London in the BlueCo era, and despite a lot of Chelsea fans being sceptical about the move, one does have to concede that he seems to be a perfect fit for new manager Alonso’s dynamic back-three system.

This is partially due to the diminutive Argentinian’s positional versatility. Barco has previously been deployed as a left back in a back four, a left wing back in a back five as well as most recently coming into his own as a left sided defensive midfielder in a double pivot.

This, along with his work-rate on the pitch, sharp footballing brain and wicked left foot have earned Barco a lot of recent attention from modern attack-minded managers, such as the new Chelsea boss who now has another excellent option in his new squad for the upcoming season.

However, currently his petulant behaviour overshadows his ability and puts any fanfare surrounding the signing on hold. Barco will have to be aware of and prepare himself for the constant abuse he is likely to receive from English fans next season.

It will be fascinating to see how the young talent responds to this inevitable criticism and how it may affect how he performs for his new club.

Sports.title: Donald Trump wins golf tournament with barely-believable score at his own course... after 'disrespectful' faux pas in front of US troops
Sports.content:
Donald Trump wins golf tournament with barely-believable score at his own course... after 'disrespectful' faux pas in front of US troops

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Donald Trump has added two more trophies to his collection after winning both the club and senior championships at his golf course in New Jersey this weekend.

Trump, 80, carded an improbably low 2-under-par score of 70 at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster over the weekend, bringing his reported tally to over 40 total victories across his various golf properties.

Social media footage showed the US President receiving a round of applause in front of the club leaderboard following the round, with a caption confirming he had collected two trophies for his performance.

The par at Bedminster is set at 72, meaning Trump allegedly finished two strokes under par to secure the double victory.

The reported 70 comes a year after the White House published a scorecard claiming Trump had carded a 3-under 69 at the same annual tournament in 2025 to win by 10 gross strokes.

Trump was seen visiting troops during his trip to New Jersey, though observers noted he was still wearing his golf glove while greeting military personnel.

Donald Trump has added two more trophies to his collection after winning both the club and senior championships at his golf course in New Jersey this weekend

Trump allegedly just won his 43rd Club Championship today at one of his courses. pic.twitter.com/8Lb8GFvnY0 — Ron Filipkowski (@RonFilipkowski) August 2, 2026

'With his golf glove on. How disrespectful,' one X user wrote in response to a video.

Another added, 'He wears his golf shoes and driving glove wherever he goes, I'm guessing....???'

The avid golfer has consistently touted his prowess on the course, declaring: 'I've played a lot, and I've played well. There are very few people who can beat me in golf.'

However, his remarkable track record and reported scores have frequently drawn skepticism from critics and sports journalists over the years.

Sportswriter Rick Reilly, who authored a book on Trump's golf habits, has previously questioned the legitimacy of his club championship wins, once stating: 'When it comes to cheating, he's an 11 on a scale of one to 10.'

Trump's outing on the course comes shortly after he said he has called off strikes on Iran 'subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL' with the Islamic regime.

The president said on Truth Social on Saturday evening that although he remains 'locked and loaded' to launch an attack, he halted the strikes in hopes of reaching a peace deal.

Trump's announcement came after reports claimed he was talked down by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over concerns that further strikes could dramatically escalate the conflict in the Middle East.

Sources told Axios that the Crown Prince urged Trump to defuse the situation, following days of tit-for-tat threats between the White House and Tehran.

Trump, 80, carded a 2-under-par score of 70 at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster

Trump visits U.S. troops in New Jersey.pic.twitter.com/fZfAZINSAS — Clash Report (@clashreport) August 1, 2026

In Trump's Truth Social post on Saturday night, he threatened to unleash 'power not seen since World War II,' but said he agreed to tentatively pause the attack.

'We have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,' Trump wrote.

'This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat.

'Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL. The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment.'

Sports.title: 5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job
Sports.content:
5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job

Gianni Infantino's job security as FIFA president has taken a huge blow following the major backlash towards his controversial plans - and efforts are being made to oust him

View 4 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi is reportedly reluctant to challenge Gianni Infantino

Gianni Infantino's days as FIFA president appear to be numbered after his plans to sell stakes in tournaments to investors backfired spectacularly.

‌



Infantino clearly misjudged the reaction to his secretive plot and could pay for the mistake with his job. UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation all voiced their displeasure with the plans, forcing Infantino to perform a humiliating U-turn.

‌



But his opponents are not satisfied with having killed the plot; they want Infantino gone following 10 years at the top of world football. UEFA are said to be 'accelerating' plans to remove the Swiss and FIFA insiders believe he is now 'certain' to go.

‌



If Infantino doesn't resign, then his opponents may have to force a vote of no confidence in his leadership, or back a rival in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. So who could put their name forward by November 18 to succeed Infantino in the election next year?

As the chiefs of world football scheme away behind the scenes, Mirror Football takes a look at five possible contenders.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Victor Montagliani

The Canadian is the CONCACAF president and has emerged as one of the main contenders in a chaotic past few days. CONCACAF rejected FIFA's proposal for private investment, but was less critical in its words than UEFA.

Montagliani is a long-time ally of Infantino's but is reportedly ready to stand against him in the elections. Before the scandal, the 60-year-old was not going to challenge Infantino - who had been set to run unopposed - but had an eye on going for the role in 2031.

Yet Infantino's sudden unpopularity has seen Montagliani sense an opportunity with his involvement in the World Cup boosting his profile and credentials. He was the first non-Caribbean CONCACAF president since 1969 when he took over and is said to have support beyond his own federation.

‌



View 4 Images CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is one of the contenders (Image: Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images)

Nasser al-Khelaifi

The Paris Saint-Germain president is one of the most powerful figures in football. The Qatari leads the European Football Clubs umbrella group and is extremely influential in European club football.

Al-Khelaifi has plenty of allies and has been suggested as the next FIFA president. The only problem is that he is reportedly not keen, with a source saying he has "absolutely no ambition, no intention, nor any interest in this role at FIFA".

‌



The chances of him changing his mind now appear even less likely after the Qatar Football Association put out a statement backing Infantino on Sunday.

View 4 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi is a powerful figure in European football (Image: LOU BENOIST/AFP via Getty Images)

Mattias Granstrom

Granstrom is the FIFA general secretary and is seen as the most likely internal candidate to step up and replace Infantino. While he lacks the profile of the other candidates, he has reportedly not been tarnished by Infantino's plan and could therefore garner support, were he to consider running.

‌



Dariusz Mioduski

The Polish lawyer is currently the vice-president of the European Football Clubs body, as well as president and owner of Legia Warsaw. His name has come up in the swirling rumour mill of the past few days

Mioduski has been backed by the Belgian, Spanish, Norwegian, German and Swedish associations, according to a report from talkSPORT earlier this month. With UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin reportedly unwilling to challenge for the FIFA presidency, Mioduski could become the European candidate.

View 4 Images Dariusz Mioduski has supporters in Europe (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sheikh Salman bin E brahim Al Khalifa

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president is another possible candidate, despite initial reluctance to step forward. The AFC released a statement saying it "stands in solidarity" with UEFA and CONCACAF, but their words were much less fiery and there is reportedly less conviction in the territory's opposition to Infantino's plans.

Al Khalifa is a Bahraini and is very experienced, having been in charge of the AFC since 2013. But it remains to seen whether the 60-year-old wants to put his name forward.

Sports.title: Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title
Sports.content:
Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title

Liverpool will hope that Andoni Iraola will be able to steady the Reds following a disastrous second season under Arne Slot but former hero Phil Thompson believes a title tilt could be on the cards

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is set to oversee his first campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool hero Phil Thompson believes the Reds could be contenders for the Premier League title under Andoni Iraola - but only if they avoid major injuries. The former Bournemouth boss was handed the reins this summer following the decision to sack Arne Slot.

‌



The Dutchman lifted the Premier League crown in his debut season at Anfield but the Merseysiders struggled to hit those heights last term. Liverpool slipped to fifth in the table, just about squeezing into the Champions League.

‌



Since then, they have lost legendary figures Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson, while Ibrahima Konate quit the club for Real Madrid. Liverpool have invested since then, sealing deals for Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, while they are chasing a big-money transfer for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola.

‌



Giving his verdict on his former side, Thompson believes that another push for the title could be on the cards should Iraola have his star players available throughout the whole season.

"Iraola will need all of his players fully fit, but if we have a fully fit squad, we have a chance of winning the league this year, without question," Thompson told the BBC. “The fans want to see a bit more aggression, but I could see, just from watching (pre-season) from the stands, the demands of the manager.

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

"Andoni wants the ball to go forward and that's what we want to see. Go forward, quicker, more precise."

‌



And while a lack of injuries might push Liverpool up the table, Thompson also believes that having vocal leaders in the dressing room might also be a useful asset under their new boss.

"When you have a difficult time — a difficult couple of games or something — you need some strong voices in there, and you just feel like there is only Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker who remain at the club," Thompson added.

"I know people go, 'Oh, Dominik Szoboszlai'. But he has only been there a couple of years. He has to step up and I think he will do.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Thompson has shared his thoughts on Liverpool ahead of the new season (Image: Getty Images)

"But there are others around the team who you look to who will have to step up, to lay down some player rules."

Liverpool have just three more pre-season friendlies to navigate against Leeds, Monaco and Como before they kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign. The Reds get themselves underway against Newcastle United away from home, before their first match at Anfield against Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut
Sports.content:
Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro endured a nightmare home debut for Inter Miami

View 2 Images Former Man Utd midfielder Casemiro had a debut to forget for Inter Miami. (Image: (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images))

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro had a home debut to forget new club Inter Miami. The Brazilian scored an own goal in the 34th minute as Inter Miami drew with the Columbus Crew.

‌



The 34 year-old played a wayward pass to the opposition, diverting the ball past his own keeper as he tried to make amends by intercepting a cross. His blunder drew the Columbus Crew level after Luis Suarez's opener in the 16th minute.

‌



Casemiro was visibly frustrated by his mistake, but Inter Miami regained the advantage before the break. Noah Allen found the net in the fifth minute of first-half added time to put the home side back in front.

‌



Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Brais Mendez scored in the 84th minute to ensure a share of the spoils with a late equaliser. Despite his blunder, Casemiro played the full 90 minutes for the second consecutive match.

His first start delivered a 1-0 victory over Montreal that was marred by a serious injury sustained by his new team-mate German Berterame.

‌



The former Real Madrid star departed Manchester United at the end of the campaign, when his contract expired. The Brazil international enjoyed an impressive final season with United but revealed his intentions to move on at the start of the year.

The experienced midfielder represented his country at the World Cup before his new club was announced following Brazil's last-16 elimination. Casemiro penned a one-year contract, with an option to prolong his stint until 2029.

View 2 Images Casemiro scored an own goal in Inter Miami's draw with Columbus Crew. (Image: (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images))

‌



Speaking earlier in the week, Casemiro disclosed he'd fantasised about lining up alongside MLS sensation Lionel Messi. The World Cup runner-up entered the fray from the substitutes' bench against Columbus to realise his former adversary's ambition.

"The amount of trouble Messi gave me. of course, I dreamed of playing with him," Casemiro said. "I always wanted to play with the best. I could never stop him, I always needed the help of my teammates.

"I am very happy to be alongside him now and I want to continue winning titles with him. I want to enjoy being alongside him, help him and make him even greater. He is one of the gods of football, if not the God of football himself, and I want to help."

‌



Casemiro's switch has arrived with its own share of controversy, though. The MLS confirmed they were examining his transfer after Inter Miami struck an agreement with LA Galaxy for the rights to secure his signature.

"The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete," the MLS said.

"While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority [first rights] to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot

A source described the FIFA President as a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor

Donald Trump addresses his call to Infantino over Balogun

Gianni Infantino looks certain to be ousted as FIFA President after his 'shabby' attempts to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



Infantino, 56, could have profited from the "Fifa Forward Enterprise" scheme (FFE) and is trying to stay in his post. But his support is flooding away.

‌



A source told the Sunday Times that Infantino is a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor.

‌



The FA and UEFA, European football's governing body, said that they had lost confidence in Infantino.

In a stinging statement, which the English FA said it supported, Uefa described the scheme as a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal he [Infantino] hatched and tried to force through".

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

View 3 Images And it's goodbye from him: Sources suggest Infantino's days at FIFA are numbered (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



It added: "The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family."

Former FA chief Mark Pallios was among those calling on Infantino to go. He said: "He should not survive.

"He has delivered these plans with a complete lack of transparency." England legend Peter Reid slammed Infantino and called for him to resign for the good of the game.

‌



He told the Mirror: "He must go - look at the World Cup: the hydration breaks for advertising, the half time show in the final.

"FIFA has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots."

CONCACAF, which governs the north and central American associations, plus the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" with Infantino's presidency.

‌



View 3 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino speaks during the 2026 World Cup draw (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident," CONCACAF said in a statement. "It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

"This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

‌



Uefa led the way in opposing the plan with its 55 members, including the FA, agreeing on Thursday to boycott all Fifa competitions.

"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game," it said.

"We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story.

‌



"The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in Fifa has only just begun."

Sources told the Sunday Times that senior figures in FIFA were looking to find a successor to Infantino.

View 3 Images Peter Reid the England legend called for Infantino to resign (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



A spokeswoman for the FA said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Infantino is likely to face an emergency FIFA council meeting where he will be asked to resign.

If he refuses, a single candidate backed by all his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year's election.

Article continues below

Candidates for the role include Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football president Sheikh Salman and Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al Khelaifi.

There may also be support for a less high-profile candidate who has backing from across the various continents.

Sports.title: Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow

The world record holder relaxed after he won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze

View 3 Images Josh Kerr with his Commonwealth Gold one mile medal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Josh Kerr joked that 'pressure is for tyres' today as he celebrated a turbo-charged Commonwealth gold in front of his home crowd in Glasgow.

The world record holder won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze. The field also included fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished fifth.

Kerr, 28, explained that he trained in the stadium as a teenager, learning how to 'win and lose'. Kerr joked that he did not feel the pressure after his world record mile two weeks ago adding: "Pressure is for tyres."

‌



View 3 Images Josh Kerr wins Commonwealth Gold in front of his home crowd (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

On being named as 'King of Scotland,' he added: "Stop it. It was incredible, the fans packed the stadium and I knew that I had to seize the moment. I learned my craft there in Scotstoun stadium, it is where I learned how to win and lose. Winning in front of the home crowd was just incredibly special."

He thanked his childhood coach and said: "I am very, very proud to be an Eric Fisher athlete." Kerr said that he hoped to set an example for young athletes. Eric, who is still coaching in Glasgow, said he was very proud to guide both Kerr and Wightman when they were teenagers.

A raucous home crowd roared with delight as Kerr took the lead in the final lap and crossed the finish line comfortably ahead of his rivals. The First Minister presented the athletes with their medals at a ceremony later in the evening.

View 3 Images Josh Kerr after his Commonwealth Gold (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Mr Swinney described Scotland’s performance in the Games as “truly historic and inspiring”. He said: “We’ve enjoyed some truly historic performances from Team Scotland at the Commonwealth Games – in swimming, bowls, athletics to name a few.

‌



“I hope that the Glasgow Games will encourage future generations to continue and build on this legacy of sporting greatness.”

The 11-day sporting extravaganza will end with tonight's closing ceremony at the Ovo Hydro. The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games has saved the British taxpayer around £600m - and may have secured the future of the event.

The total public funding allocated to stage the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games was £778 million. Birmingham City Council and local partners contributed £184m (25%) of that total.

The remaining 75% (£594m) was covered by the UK central government. Organisers of Glasgow 2026 say that using hotels instead of a village, along with smaller arenas and fewer events, cut costs to around £160m. Victoria in Australia was due to host the event and paid £199m to pull out which has funded Glasgow 2026 without taxpayers paying a penny.

Phil Batty, the chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: “This definitely isn’t the last hurrah for the Commonwealth Games. What we’ve seen is a wholesale shift in what the Commonwealth Games needs to do to sustain itself, not just through 2030, but through 2034, 2038 and beyond."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
